articleTitle: Progress towards mobile ultra-stable lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: It is reported on new results in creation of highly stable lasers including compact diode-pumped crystal lasers with narrow radiation line and high long-term frequency stability (of the order of 10/sup -13/-10/sup -14/). The immediate prospects of creation of lasers with long-term stability and frequency reproducibility at the level of 10/sup -16/-10/sup -17/ are considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High accuracy low-voltage ac-dc transfer standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Micropotentiometers and resistive dividers are designed using thick-film chip resistors. Two methods to determine the ac-dc transfer difference at low voltages using micropotentiometers and resistive dividers are described. At 10 mV, the difference between the two methods are less than 10 ppm at 1 kHz and less than 100 ppm at 1 MHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microcalorimetric measurement of the effective efficiency of microwave power sensors comprising thermocouples
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new method to calibrate thermoelectric power sensors is established and investigated, where the effective efficiency is directly determined in a microcalorimeter. A commercially available power-thermovoltage converter (power sensor) without any electronics is used. The results show good agreement with results obtained by comparing the sensor with a calibrated thermistor mount, and smaller uncertainties.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An electrometric method for precise ac/dc transfer measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A proposal for a new electrometric method for high precision ac/dc transfer measurements is described It is based on a high resolution analytical balance and on a suitable automatic control of the distance and the parallelism between the electrodes detected by means of capacitive sensors. Possible sources of ac/dc transfer difference are identified and an evaluation of their effects is reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A miniature optically pumped cesium beam resonator: first results
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The main characteristics of a miniature optically pumped cesium beam resonator (OPCsBR) are described. An evaluation of the frequency stability performances of this device is presented. Moreover, the dependence of the symmetry of the microwave spectrum on the laser detuning is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Zeeman coherences and dark states in optically pumped cesium frequency standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We develop a model for optically trapped states including Zeeman coherences to show that their number depends only on the change in F (hyperfine state) during the transition and is independent of the polarization or the coordinate system. Using a polarization switching technique, we achieve complete optical pumping even in the small magnetic field used in our primary standard.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A computer-controlled current-comparator-based load loss standard for calibrating high-voltage power measurement systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A computer-controlled load loss standard, based on the current-comparator technique, for calibrating high-voltage power measurement systems is described. Measurements can be made at any power factor from zero lag through unity to zero lead, positive or negative power, at voltages up to 100 kV, currents up to 1000 A, and 50 or 60 Hz. The load loss standard features current-comparator-based components including a high-voltage active divider, a unity-gain integrator for producing an accurate and stable reactive component, a high-current transconductance amplifier with the ability to provide a highly accurate current to a circuit that is operated at high voltage, and a computer for control and data reduction. The load loss standard has accuracies of better than 500 ppm in magnitude and 20 ppm in phase.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A very low frequency ac-dc transfer standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A low frequency ac-dc transfer standard has been developed to satisfy the NML demand for very low frequency ac-dc transfer calibrations. Tests performed using digitally synthesised signals and synchronised precision dc measurements showed less than 30 ppm change in the ac-dc difference of the standard in the frequency range 0.01-100 Hz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power stabilised exceptionally high stability cryogenic sapphire resonator oscillator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Power stabilized microwave oscillators of exceptional short term stability have been realized from cryogenic sapphire resonators with loaded Q-factors of 10/sup 9/ at X-band and 6 K. These oscillators have exhibited a fractional frequency stability of 3-4/spl times/10/sup -15/ for integration times from 0.3 to 100 seconds degrading to 10/sup -14/ at 1000 seconds.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A measuring system for calibration of power analyzers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A digital sampling watt meter has been designed for calibration of power analyzers. The watt meter is based on two commercially available sampling DVMs. The power spectrum is calculated with DFT analysis. High accuracy is achieved by phase locking and simultaneous sampling.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Non-destructive permittivity measurement of substrates
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The permittivity of a thin flat dielectric is calculated from the characteristics of the H-011 resonance in a cylindrical cavity with the specimen inserted an the central transverse plane. Dielectric constants from 1 to 300 and loss tangents as low as 30/spl plusmn/10 ppm have been determined. No irreversible specimen preparation is required.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new VLBI data acquisition and processing system, K-4
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have been developed a new VLBI system applicable to VLBA and VSOP. This system has been achieved by using a high speed A/D, digital filter and 32 MHz IRM. An XF type correlation processor has been developed by making use of field programmable gate array.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experimental determinations of the quantity M//spl rho/ for silicon single crystals used in the determination of the Avogadro constant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Considerable improvements in the measurements of the molar mass M(Si) of silicon crystals combined with high-accuracy densities (/spl rho/) of the same crystals, have yielded experimental M(Si)//spl rho/ values resulting from the PTB-IRMM, the IMGC-IRMM and the NRLM-IRMM projects for the redetermination of Avogadro's Constant. These M(Si)//spl rho/ values are compared with attributed uncertainties, in relation to the supposition of constancy M(Si)//spl rho/ for silicon.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated thin-film micropotentiometers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Integrated micropotentiometers, new devices fabricated with thin-film technology and the micromachining of silicon, have been developed for the accurate determination of ac voltage from 1 to 200 mV up to 100 kHz and with the potential for higher frequencies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High performance near field measurements for antennas and microstrip circuits
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A simple and efficient computer-controlled setup for measuring near fields has been realized. It uses the modulated scatterer technique, together with a homodyne receiver to measure both the amplitude and phase of the fields. To move the probe, a standard plotter is used. Special probes have been designed for measuring all field components.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Vectorial calibration of 3-D magnetic field sensor arrays
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Measuring devices for field structure analysis or the vectorial measurement of field distributions must be calibrated vectorially in three axis. This paper presents and compares two procedures for the calibration of sensor arrays. The measurements used for this are derived from a solenoid coil, which can be calibrated by the Physikalische Technisch Bundesanstallt PTB.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A potential new frequency/wavelength standard at 778 nm: Doppler free two-photon transitions in rubidium
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have stabilized two laser diodes on the hyperfine components of the 5D/sub 3/2/ and 5D/sub 5/2/ two-photon transitions in natural rubidium (v=385 THz). We have carefully investigated the metrological features of these devices. So far we obtain a frequency stability in terms of the Allan variance of 3.10/sup -13/./spl tau//sup - 1/2 / up to 2000 s and a frequency repeatability of the order of 10/sup -12/. The frequency difference between the two devices is 1.7 kHz under identical operating conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Programmable digitally synthesized source for low-frequency calibrations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A digitally synthesized source (DSS) designed to calibrate low-frequency (0.1 Hz to 1 kHz) digital voltmeters and thermal converters is described. The DSS output voltage, frequency, and waveform are programmable over the General Purpose Interface Bus (GPIB). The rms value of the output voltage is calculated, with an uncertainty of less than 5 ppm, by measuring the dc voltage of each of the steps used to create the waveform.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of multilayer thin-film multijunction thermal converters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: New multilayer, thin-film multijunction thermal converters (MJTCs) suitable as high performance ac-dc transfer standards have been fabricated and studied at NIST. This paper describes their thermal and physical features and the materials chosen to improve performance. Performance data are given over a wide range of frequencies and conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Error corrected impedance measurements with a network analyzer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: For a network analyzer some error corrected impedance or two-port measurements are presented. These ZU and YU self-calibration procedures only need one known and one or two unknown impedances for the calibration process. The good performance of these simple methods is demonstrated by experimental results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement performance of a millimetric dual six-port network analyzer in the W frequency band (75-110 GHz)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper presents the measurement performances of a dual six-port network analyzer in the W frequency band (75-110 GHz) using Schottky diodes as power detectors. A "LRL" and another calibration technique are used to determine the full scattering parameters of the DUT. Finally, a comparison between experimental results, in reflection and transmission, performed with the six-port network analyzer and the other measurement systems available in the W frequency band is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel microwave fatigue crack detection technique using an open-ended coaxial line
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Surface crack detection on metallic structures (aircraft fuselage, turbine blades and nuclear power plant steam generator turbines) is of utmost importance. The use of an open-ended coaxial line for this purpose is very attractive because it offers advantages such as a wide frequency band of operation, small aperture (sensing) area, and excellent sensitivity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Directly time domain antenna measurement technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This work summarizes the experience of time-domain direct measurements which has been accumulated at the Radiophysical Research Institute for the last 9 years. The various aspects of the method of far field time domain signal restoration by the measurements of near field time domain antenna response are the focus of the paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A thin-film dual heater ac-dc converter with infrared sensor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A dual heater isothermal converter for precise ac-dc transfer is realized by using thin-film heaters on a thin sandwich membrane, and by sensing their temperature with an infrared pyrometer. This reduces diversion of heat from the heaters, the thermal time-constant and the ac-dc transfer differences due to thermoelectric effects, shunt capacitances and dielectric losses.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high sensitivity sapphire transducer for vibration measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this report we describe an interferometric sapphire dielectric resonator (SDR) transducer which avoids the need for an ultra low noise oscillator. An initial performance of the transducer is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Diode lasers for precision spectroscopy of calcium
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Diode lasers at 657 nm are used with an atomic beam and a high-flux calcium beam-cell to provide narrow saturated-absorption resonances. Stability of /spl ap/3/spl times/10/sup -14//spl tau//sup 1/2 / is projected based on signal-to-noise ratios. Laser cooling is possible with a frequency doubled diode laser system that produces a usable 35 mW at 423 nm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A de-embedding technique for reflection-based S-parameters measurements of microwave devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A generalized calibration and de-embedding technique for reflection-based S-parameter measurements of microwave devices is proposed. This technique allows to perform the two-port calibration of a network analyzer directly from the embedded reflection coefficient measurements. This technique is a general one, in the sense that it can be implemented in network analyzers with or without transmission measurement capabilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Metrological applications of single electron tunneling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Recent progress on Coulomb blockade devices allows charge to be determined by counting electrons. These devices eventually may give a new intrinsic standard of capacitance and a new measurement of the fine structure constant. The author explains the requirements of three important components of such an experiment: the charge pump, the electrometer, and the cryogenic fixed capacitor. The performance of this standard is limited by the ability to transfer electrons through the electron pump with very small errors. He discussses an experiment in which a 5-junction pump was operated with an error for transferring electrons of approximately 0.5 ppm. The error predicted from existing theory is several orders of magnitude smaller, thus implying that the usual understanding of the Coulomb blockade is incomplete. It is deduced that the errors arise from photon-assisted tunneling, where the photon energy is supplied from the environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The NPL moving-coil watt balance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We describe progress since the 1992 CPEM towards linking the electrical to the mechanical watt with less than 1 in 10/sup 8/ uncertainty to measure Planck's constant and monitor the stability of the kilogram.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Leading logarithmic corrections to the muonium hyperfine splitting and to the hydrogen Lamb shift
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Main leading corrections with recoil logarithm log(M/m) and low-energy logarithm log(Z/spl alpha/) to the Muonium hyperfine splitting are discussed. Logarithmic corrections have magnitudes of 0.1/spl divide/0.3 kHz. Non-leading higher order corrections are expected to be not larger than 0.1 kHz. Leading logarithmic correction to the Hydrogen Lamb shift is also obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quadrature bridge for the comparison of quantum Hall resistors with capacitors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A quadrature bridge for the comparison of two quantized Hall resistances R/sub H/(2)=12906.4035 /spl Omega/ and two 10 nF capacitances is described The bridge was designed for a high-precision determination of the von Klitzing constant in SI units, based on a realisation of the farad via the Thompson-Lampard capacitor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved vacuum thermocouples
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Prior construction of single junction vacuum thermal convertors (SJTCs) did not consistently produce units with AC-DC differences of a few ppm or less. Four improvement modes have been introduced. (1) Elimination of flaming during the making of the mounting bead. (2) Changing of the feed-through posts from Dumet to platinum-iridium. (3) Decrease of the Thomson coefficient by changing from nickel-chromium to Evanohm heater wire. (4) Lowering of the temperature gradient along the heater wire in the vicinity of the thermocouple. SJTCs can now be constructed with AC-DC differences of less than 0.3 ppm at a high yield.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and optimization of range resistors for a multijunction thermal converter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The range resistors to be used with a multijunction thermal converter (MJTC) have been developed. Based on the measured frequency dependence of the impedance of the PTB-type VJTCC an appropriate model for the converter has been developed. Range resistors have been designed in such a way that the voltage across the thermal converter remains unchanged from dc to 1 MHz within a few ppm. The stray capacitance of the resistors is blocked with active guards and the skin effect is compensated with a family of the RC-circuits set in parallel with the range resistor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Precision automated capacitance bridges for the low frequency range at the PTB
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Two computer-controlled capacitance bridges for different fields of application have been developed at the PTB. The first one, the universal bridge, works in the capacitance range of less than 1 pF up to 1 /spl mu/F and in a frequency range up to 1 kHz, The total calculated relative uncertainties (2/spl sigma/) are in the order of 5/spl middot/10/sup -6/ and 20/spl middot/10/sup -6/. The second one, the fixed ratio bridge, calibrates primary standards with capacitance values from 1 pF to 1 nF in 1:1, 1:2, 1:5 or 1:10 steps at frequencies from 100 Hz to 10 kHz. The relative uncertainty of one 1:10 step at a frequency of 1592 Hz is estimated to be 3/spl middot/10/sup -8/ (1/spl sigma/).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Applications of a multi-state termination to microwave metrology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Although the automated vector network analyzer (ANA) was introduced to the microwave community more than two decades ago, the accuracy assessment of these devices has been a continuing challenge to the national metrology laboratories. The application of a multi-state two-port to this problem has generated a large amount of interest. This paper reviews this development and outlines additional applications for this technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improvements in the realization of the quantized-Hall resistance standard at OFMET
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A measurement system based on a cryogenic current comparator has been developed at the Swiss Federal Office of Metrology (OFMET) to maintain the electrical unit of resistance. Standard resistors in the range of 1 /spl Omega/ to 10 k/spl Omega/ can be measured against the quantized Hall resistance with a precision on the order of one part in 10/sup 9/(ppb). This system improves the measurement accuracy of OFMET in this range by one order of magnitude.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Josephson D/A converter with fundamental accuracy [voltage standard]
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A binary sequence of series arrays of shunted Josephson junctions is used to make a 14-bit D/A converter. With thirteen bias lines any step number in the range -8192 to +8192 (1.2 to -1.2 V) can be selected in the time required to stabilize the bias current (a few microseconds). The circuit makes possible the digital synthesis of very-accurate ac waveforms whose amplitude derives directly from the internationally accepted definition of the volt.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Advancements in picosecond resolution time interval measurement techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: New, efficient measurement techniques are used to adequately characterize the actual performance of the new generation of programmable equivalent time sequential sampling oscilloscopes. These instruments provide new time interval measurement capabilities with increased repeatability and accuracy. Subpicosecond repeatability for risetime measurements of fast step generators (20 ps transition time) has been observed. A typical timebase related peak error of 3 ps for short time interval measurements (up to tens of ns) has been shown. A brief introduction on the horizontal timebase error sources is followed by the description of the automated measurement techniques. Finally actual measurement results are shown using the described techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Antenna measurements: a comparison of far-field, compact range and near-field techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Current state of the art in precision antenna measurements is discussed for three commonly employed antenna measurement systems, far-field, near-field, and compact ranges. We begin with a review of antenna test types and requirements and continue with a discussion issues and challenges which have recently arisen to antenna test and measurement. Each measurement technique, is then discussed including the limitations and advantages of each. In fact, each technique is uniquely qualified to produce high quality measurements of specific but different applications. These specific applications are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A low-current precision DC, AC and DC/AC clamp-on measurement sensor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A low-current precision DC, AC and DC/AC clamp-on measurement sensor is described that can be used to make on-line calibration and measurement of DC, AC and DC/AC low-current in industry and laboratory. The sensor features current ratio accuracy grade of better than (5/spl sim/10)/spl times/10/sup -4/ for 10/spl sim/200 amperes current range, current resolution of 0.01 ampere, and transient response time of less than 1/spl times/10/sup -3/ second for the DC, AC and DC/AC clamp-on prototype.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A globally efficient and effective means of maintaining the SI second and UTC time
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Time and frequency quality comparable to the best laboratories has been demonstrated on an integrated system suitable for field application on a global basis. The integration consists of a new commercial primary cesium-beam frequency standard technology, an ensemble algorithm optimally combining the times of these standards, and an optimum filtering of the signal from the GPS satellites.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated micromachined accurate electrostatic true rms-to-dc converter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The rms value gives the average energy content of a signal, which is an important parameter in measurements of electrical signals. For non-sinusoidal signals of arbitrary shape a true rms converter should be used. From the existing converters, like electronic, thermal, electrodynamic and electrostatic types, only electronic and thermal converters have been monolithically integrated to date. With the development of micromachining techniques it is possible to integrate also the electrostatic converter. Merging this micromachined converter with on-chip readout electronics enables an accurate converter to be realised when placed in a feedback loop.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: AC measurements of the quantized Hall resistance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The quantized Hall resistance R/sub H/(i), for i=2, 4 and 6 has been measured in the frequency range from DC to 3 kHz by a standard four terminal-pair impedance bridge. For frequencies f, less than 2 kHz, the relative error /spl epsi/(i) between the AC and DC values appeared to be proportional to f and to increase as i decreased. /spl epsi/(6) appeared to be less than 0.4 ppm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric properties of materials at cryogenic temperatures and microwave frequencies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The permittivity and dielectric loss tangent of single-crystal quartz, cross-linked polystyrene (Rexolite), and polytetrafluoroethylene (Teflon) were measured at microwave frequencies and at temperatures of 77 K and 300 K using a dielectric resonator technique. Application of high-temperature superconducting (HTS) films as the endplates of the dielectric resonator made it possible to determine dielectric loss tangents of about 7/spl times/10/sup 6/ at 77 K. Two permittivity tensor components for uniaxially anisotropic crystalline quartz were measured. Although the permittivities at 77 K changed very little from their room temperature values at 300 K, large changes in dielectric losses were observed. The decreased loss characteristics of these microelectronic substrates can markedly improve the performance of many microwave devices at cryogenic temperatures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Resistance scaling up to 1 M/spl Omega/ at PTB with a cryogenic current comparator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A cryogenic current comparator (CCC) of the Delahaye-type is used to scale the unit of resistance between 1 /spl Omega/ and 1 M/spl Omega/ in terms of R/sub K-90/. Measurements are demonstrated to check the accuracy and reproducibility of the system. Especially for the values above 10 k/spl Omega/ the uncertainty of the maintained standards could be reduced by more than one order of magnitude compared to conventional scaling methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: AC-DC difference characteristics of high-voltage thermal voltage converters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a study of thermal voltage converters (TVCs) at voltages above 500 V and at frequencies up to 100 kHz. The effects of aging and dielectric loss on the resistor, as well as changes in the timing sequence of AC-DC difference tests, relay dead-times, warmup times and voltage level dependence are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The silicon-28 path to the Avogadro constant-first experiments and outlook
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The first investigations of lattice parameter, density and molar mass of an enriched silicon 28 single crystal are reported. The unexpectedly large amount of impurity atoms in the material at present limits the goal of improving the uncertainty in a new determination of the Avogadro constant.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An accurate, self-checking digital teraohmmeter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We describe a new digital teraohmmeter achieving state-of-the-art linearity and long-term stability through the application of automatic self-checking circuits and routines. To ensure its voltage-independence up to 1000 V and <100 ppm linearity in measuring 10/sup 5/ to 10/sup 15/ /spl Omega/ (at /spl ges/1 pA), internal scaling and timing circuits have been upgraded for higher speed and better performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automated measurement of capacitance from 500 pF to 40 mF
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a method of deriving capacitance from current, voltage and time measurement with high accuracy over a wide range. The method was developed to provide automated traceable measurement of the continuously variable capacitance function of a newly developed calibrator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A study of the stability of some Zener-diode based voltage standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report on a study of factors limiting the precision of Zener-diode based electronic voltage standards of the type the most widely used at the highest levels of accuracy in national metrology institutes. Frequency-dependent noise is the major factor limiting short-term stability to about one part in 10/sup 8/. Medium- and long-term stability is severely limited by humidity effects; variations of relative humidity of 0.01 can cause changes of 0.1 /spl mu/V or more in the 1.018 V output.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Determination of the fine structure constant by measuring the quotient of the Planck constant and the neutron mass
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In the silicon crystal the (331) reflection was used. The reflected neutrons had a wavelength of 0.249 nm corresponding to a velocity of 1590 ms/sup -1/. The wavelength follows from the lattice parameter of the silicon crystal. This was measured at the PTB by comparing it with the lattice parameters of the reference silicon crystal. The principle of the velocity measurement is as follows: a roughly monochromatic beam of polarized neutrons is produced by Bragg reflection in a magnetised crystal of Heusler alloy. The beam is modulated by periodically changing the direction of the polarization vector, the frequency being about 750 kHz. For this purpose, a novel type of modulator is used called a meander coil. It produces a magnetic field which is periodic in time and space. After a flight path of several meters the neutrons are incident on the silicon crystal mentioned above. Those with the correct wavelength are back-reflected and returned to the modulator. Here, the beam is again modulated and the two modulations are superposed. The resulting total modulation is analysed by the Bragg reflection in a second magnetised crystal of Heusler alloy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Uncertainties of the NIST coaxial noise calibration system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Uncertainties of the NIST broadband coaxial calibration system are analyzed. The expanded relative uncertainty for a source with the ENR of /spl ap/15 dB is typically 1.6%.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A sensor self-heating method for lead's resistance compensation in two wires RTD's measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper shows a new method to compensate large lead's resistance influence in two wires RTD (resistance temperature sensor) temperature measurements. A time sharing sensor self-heating technique is provided to accomplish an accurate temperature acquisition for industrial or laboratory research.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of the 10-V Josephson junction array at ETL
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The 10-V Josephson junction array has been developed at ETL. The array with 20144 junctions aligned on 4 branches of strip line generates quantized voltage steps up to 13.8 V under millimeter-wave irradiation of 90 mW and 94 GHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Anomalous magnetic moment of the muon and hyperfine structure and Zeeman effect in ground state muonium
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The aim of the ongoing muon g-2 experiment at Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL) to measure a/sub /spl mu// to 0.35 ppm represents a factor of 20 improvement over the current value obtained from the latest CERN experiment. This projected precision would allow us to determine the electroweak contribution, involving single loop Feynman diagrams of W, Z and Higgs scalar particle, to a/sub /spl mu// with an accuracy of about 20%. Coupled with improvements in the QED theoretical calculation for a/sub /spl mu// and the completion of associated experiments needed to improve the calculation of the hadronic contribution to a/sub /spl mu//, a comparison of a/sub /spl mu//(expt) and a/sub /spl mu//(theor) will provide a sensitive test of the standard model concerning renormalizability of the electroweak theory, and to search for physics beyond the standard model with high sensitivity especially for investigating lepton substructures, which would be complementary to the current and future high energy collider experiments including LHC and LEP II. A new high precision measurement of the muonium (/spl mu//sup +/e/sup -/) hyperfine structure interval /spl Delta//spl nu/ and its Zeeman effect in the ground state which gives the muon magnetic moment is being undertaken at the Los Alamos Meson Physics Facility (LAMPF). The goal of the experiment is to measure the ratio of the magnetic moments of muon and proton to a fractional accuracy of 60 parts per billion (ppb), and the muonium hyperfine structure interval in the ground state, /spl Delta//spl nu/, to 10 ppb. These measurements will improve our knowledge of /spl mu//sub /spl mu////spl mu//sub p/ and /spl Delta//spl nu/ by a factor of about 5. With the improved accuracy in /spl mu//sub /spl mu////spl mu//sub p/ to 60 ppb from LAMPF, /spl Delta//spl nu//sub expt/ and /spl Delta//spl nu//sub theor/ could be compared at about the 65 ppb level. This would be the most precise test of a two-lepton bound state system and of bound state QED in general. Alternatively, the fine structure constant a could be determined at the 30 ppb level. A precise value for /spl mu//sub /spl mu////spl mu//sub p/ is needed for the determination of the anomalous g-factor from the new Brookhaven muon g-2 experiment. New values for electric charges of positive and negative muons and the magnetic moment of the negative muon will be presented. The experiment to determine the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon is being prepared by the Muon (g-2) Collaboration. The muonium experiment is being carried out by collaborators from the Experiment 1054 at LAMPF. The status of the two experiments will be described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of quantum Hall effect resistance standards of the BNM/LCIE and the BIPM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A comparison of quantum Hall effect (QME) resistance standards has been carried out by transporting a complete QHE system from the BIPM to the Laboratoire Primaire d'Electricite-Magnetisme (BNM/LCIE). From 13 to 17 December 1993, measurements of a 100 /spl Omega/ resistance standard were carried out with the QHE standards of the two laboratories. The results agree to within a few parts in 10/sup 9/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new self-calibrating standard instrument for current transformer calibration
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new current comparator-based self-calibrating instrument for current transformer calibration has been developed. The instrument measures the in-phase and quadrature components of the error by means of a digital vector voltmeter. The built-in ratio matching unit makes it possible to compare current transformers of different ratios. A set of built-in auxiliary windings ensure complete on-site self-testing of the instrument. The ratio matching unit can be tested and calibrated by the anti-offset method. The basic accuracy of the instrument is 2 ppm with 0.1 ppm resolution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Different schemes and structure of the accuracy budget in cesium frequency standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Many systematic effects have been identified, which can shift the frequency of Cs standards from the ideal frequency of the unperturbed hyperfine separation. They limit the accuracy with which the definition of the second is realized to the uncertainty at which they can be evaluated. The list of known systematics is reviewed in this paper in a critical way, by looking at the nonlinear interaction which occurs among the various effects in the design stage. Consideration is given to several different configurations from the point of view of accuracy analysis and the kind of interplay that ties the various systematic effects. It is the author's opinion that all these schemes are valid and should be independently perfected. In fact, the quality of the realization of the definition of a fundamental unit is a matter of accuracy, and type B uncertainties-are therefore the limit. Building more standards does not seem to be the correct approach in an effort toward the improvement of the realization of the second. More convincing appears the idea to build and perfect more different types of standards, with a different set of systematics and different interplay among them. In this way the risk of overlooking technological "phase lock" and undesired human coherence should be minimized, and the independence of different realizations of the second best guaranteed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new millisecond pulsar observation system at CRL
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The Communications Research Laboratory (CRL) has developed an unique system using an acousto-optic spectrometer for precise timing measurements for millisecond pulsars. This system can treat a signal of 50 MHz bandwidth, have a frequency resolution of 200 kHz and a time resolution of 13 /spl mu/s, and average 2/sup 24/ pulses without dead time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An automatic procedure for a calibration of a network analyzer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An automatically controlled calibration procedure will be presented which is based on a virtual transformation of calibration standards. The basic element is a switching network added to the network analyzer. This network is a part of the analyzer, so it will not be removed after the calibration has been finished. It is not necessary to know the characteristics of the single switching states. Compared with commercially available procedures the expense of the new calibration technique is decreased.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Resonant frequencies and Q factors of dielectric parallelepipeds by measurement and by FDTD
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the measurement and computation of the resonant frequencies and the associated Q factors of dielectric parallelepipeds made of high-permittivity, low-loss ceramic materials. Each resonance peak is measured separately with a fine frequency step. A curve-fitting method is used to accurately estimate the resonant frequency and 3 dB bandwidth from the somewhat noisy measured data. The finite-difference time-domain method is used to compute the initial portion of the backscattered field due to a Gaussian pulse plane wave. The time response is then extended to zero value by Prony's method. The measured and computed data is compared for a parallelepiped resonator of permittivity 37.84.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wavelet analysis for synchronization and timekeeping
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Results are presented of wavelet analysis as applied to loop-back phase measurements of a high precision NIST-developed modem used for satellite two-way time transfer. It is also applied to phase measurements between a high-performance Cs and H-maser clock.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Proposal of up-to-date standards on methods of measuring noise in linear two-ports
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: One of the most interesting topics for microwave community is the characterization of low-noise transistors. After so many years, the standards suggested by IEEE in 1960 are considered obsolete by the experimenters. A new methodology is proposed here as a standard. To support this proposal, an original measuring system for the complete characterization of microwave transistors in terms of noise, gain and scattering parameters from noise figure measurements only is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An analysis of some errors of antenna patterns restored by measurements on near zone plane
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The goal of the paper is to analyze some planar near-field measurement errors associated with the fact that the field is really measured at some distance from the aperture while the Fourier transform used for antenna pattern restoration is valid only for measurements made on the aperture itself.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis and calculation of magnetic shielding effectiveness for comparators
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A method of analyzing and calculating magnetic shielding effectiveness of comparators by means of long rectangular shell model with a magnetic core is developed. The calculation formula is derived. The error between testing results and calculation data for the magnetic shielding effectiveness of 25,000-ampere dc comparator is less than 5 percent.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rabi pedestal shifts as a diagnostic tool for primary frequency standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have measured the small shifts of the Rabi pedestals relative to the narrow Ramsey fringes in NIST's new optically-pumped frequency standard. The dependence of these shifts on magnetic field, Zeeman line, and microwave power enables us to analyze the frequency biases in the standard resulting from Rabi pulling, cavity pulling, and magnetic field inhomogeneity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement of complex permittivity of materials using an open-ended coaxial probe: test of an analytic model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A method is presented for determining the complex permittivity of materials using an open-ended coaxial probe. A two-dimensional second-order rational polynomial function is used to construct the aperture admittance. The inverse problem of determining permittivity reduces to the solution of a quadratic equation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Progress report on the linear ion trap extended (LITE)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We discuss an improved architecture for a small ion trap based frequency standard. This design will reduce the size and cost of current Hg/sup +/ standards and improve the long term frequency stability. Based on our earlier work, stability of 7/spl times/10/sup -14///spl radic//spl tau/ is anticipated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of the dual heater isothermal AC/DC converter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The dual heater isothermal AC/DC converter recently introduced by Katzmann (1989) was developed and tested experimentally. This analysis shows that the device used in a negative feedback loop, driven by a sinusoidal voltage, does yield the RMS value and shows the major sources and approximate magnitudes of error.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical detector nonlinearity: a comparison of five methods
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We derived a set of unified equations for five methods to evaluate nonlinearity of power meters and detectors. We performed computer simulations of these methods. The simulations assist in design of a measurement system to meet a target accuracy. Measurements verified the simulations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New Zealand's 1 V Josephson array voltage standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the fully automatic one volt Josephson array voltage standard that has been commissioned as New Zealand's standard of dc voltage.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A transfer device for 10 V Josephson array measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: To improve measurements of 10 V Zener based standards, we have designed a new transfer voltage source for use with 10 V Josephson arrays. The transfer voltage is compared, in turn, with that of the Zener standard and of the array. The use of two separate circuits should help to solve the problem of common ground connections and prevent noise from the Zener standard entering the array circuit. This transfer device can also be used for 10 V Josephson array comparisons.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement of the absolute frequency of molecular iodine transitions near 532 nm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The optical frequencies of several transitions in iodine have been measured using the D2 line in Rb 780 nm and an iodine-stabilized 633 nm He-Ne laser. This measurement provides a useful, stable and highly reproducible optical frequency reference in the green.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: AC measurements of the residual longitudinal resistivity of different GaAs-based samples in the QHE regime between 3 Hz and 100 kHz
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: AC measurements of the longitudinal resistivity, /spl rho//sub xx/, of three QHE samples were made at frequencies up to 100 kHz, at 1.2 K and 4.3 K, on the i=1.2 and 4 plateaus. Preliminary results show a frequency dependence on the residual value of the minimum of /spl rho//sub xx/, /spl rho//sub xx//sup min/, but not, or very few on the width of the magnetic flux density range over which /spl rho//sub xx//sup min/ takes place. In the frequency domain around 1 kHz, the /spl rho//sub xx//sup min/ values lie within 0.4 m/spl Omega/ to 8 m/spl Omega/ at 1.2 K, depending on plateaus and samples used. It promises an expected quantization of the Hall resistance, /spl rho//sub xy/=R/sub H/(i), to be complete at a level of one part in 10/sup 8/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Vibrational phase analysis of multipoints on vibrating object using laser-diode displacement meters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Vibrational displacement waveforms of two points on vibrating body are directly and simultaneously measured using two sets of digital displacement meter, which employs self-mixing laser Doppler velocimeter. Frequency spectrum and phase of the displacement are computer analyzed. This method is useful to construct compact and inexpensive vibration analysis system for multipoints.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A possibility of reducing the effect of interrogation phase noise on the frequency stability in passive frequency standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Due to an intermodulation effect, the local oscillator phase noise may limit the medium term frequency stability of passive frequency standards. A new possibility of reducing this effect is presented. The mathematical approach is confirmed by a simulation of the frequency standard behavior. Optimal demodulation waveforms are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new method to measure silicon lattice spacings and possible new definition of the kilogram: scheme and progress
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: For possible new definition of the kilogram, we propose to use picometer metrology and AFM to continuously scan with atomic resolution a surface strip of about 2 nm/spl times/10 mm area on a single silicon crystal in a 2/spl times/10/sup -11/ torr vacuum chamber to measure silicon lattice spacings to 0.1-1 ppb.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The IMGC volume-density standards for the Avogadro constant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Within the project for the determination of the Avogadro constant, the IMGC has developed volume-density standards in the form of single-crystal silicon spheres. In addition to a first sphere previously characterised and intercompared with a similar artifact, a new sphere of nearly perfect form is now available. The absolute determination of its mass and volume is presented together with the expected improvements in the assignment of a density value to high-purity and near-perfect silicon single-crystals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: International comparison GT-RF 75A4: reflection coefficient in 14 mm/50 ohm coaxial line at 0.5 GHz, 3 GHz and 7 GHz
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The results are presented of an international comparison of measurements of the complex reflection coefficient in the G 900-14 mm/50 ohm coaxial line at 0.5 GHz, 3 GHz and 7 GHz in which eleven national laboratories of metrology participated. The standards showed very small drifts of the reflection coefficient during a period of nine years. With few exceptions, good agreement between the mean values reported by the different participants is observed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mass spectrometry at and below 0.1 parts per billion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The single ion Penning trap mass spectrometer at M.I.T. can compare masses to within 0.1 parts per billion. We have created a short table of fundamental atomic masses and made measurements useful for calibrating the X-ray standard, and determining Avogadro's number, the molar Plank constant, and the fine structure constant.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison between a vector multiport network analyzer and the national S-parameter: measurement system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A multiport vector network analyzer based on a new calibration concept, has been compared with the P-port S-parameter National measurement system at IENGF. The measurements were performed on precision 7 mm standard components and exhibited an optimum agreement. These results open the possibility to use the new multiport network analyzer for certification measurements of multiport devices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Compound material for electromagnetic shielding in electrical and cryoelectronical applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A compound material based on aluminum and amorphous, soft magnetic alloys has been developed by means of glueing techniques which are commonly used in aerospace applications to produce metallic or fibrous laminates. It is well suited for the construction of high-quality shielding containers against electromagnetic fields from dc to some 100 kHz. Its magnetic properties can be modified over a wide range by varying the number and the thickness of the laminate. The magnetic properties are not affected by mechanical working processes, such as turning, cutting or drilling.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calibration of inductive voltage dividers at extremely low frequencies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A measuring arrangement based on digital compensators is described which can be used to determine the complex division factor D_ of inductive voltage dividers (IVD) at extremely low frequencies. The error of division at 1 Hz, related to the division factor D_ at 32 Hz was evaluated as 18.7 ppm/spl plusmn/3.3 ppm (1/spl sigma/) in magnitude and -4.5 m/spl deg//spl plusmn/0.42 m/spl deg/(1/spl sigma/) in phase for an IVD selected as an example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a fast-reversed-dc current source
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A fast-reversed-dc current source has been developed for the purpose of evaluating the ac-dc transfer differences due to thermoelectric effect of thermal converters. By use of a novel switching scheme, the measurement error due to the increase of the reversing frequency was reduced to less than 1 ppm up to 10 kHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The proposed use of GPS to provide the frequency traceability for a Josephson Array Voltage Standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A Josephson Array Voltage Standard (JAVS) has been established at the National Metrology Laboratory (NML) in South Africa, with the assistance of NIST and the PTB. We are currently working on what we believe to be the first use of the global positioning system (GPS) to provide direct frequency traceability for a JAVS.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved determination of fine structure constant based on the electron g-2 and muonium hyperfine structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper reports two new determinations of the fine structure constant /spl alpha/ based on quantum electrodynamics (QED). One byproduct is a substantial improvement in the precision of muon rest mass.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Relative accuracy of isolated and unisolated noise comparison radiometers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A rigorous radiometer equation is derived and used to develop better corrections and uncertainty estimates. Isolated and well corrected unisolated radiometers have similar accuracies for low reflection coefficient sources. To ignore corrections for the finite isolation of a radiometer, about 38 dB isolation is needed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Intercomparisons of Josephson Array Voltage Standards: EUROMET project 199
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Eight intercomparisons of Josephson Array Voltage Standard (JAVS) systems of Denmark, BIPM, Netherlands, Germany, France, Sweden, Spain and Israel have been performed. For most comparisons full calibration systems were compared using a Zener reference standard as transfer source.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Audio-frequency analysis of inductive voltage dividers based on structural models
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A binary inductive voltage divider (BIVD) is compared with a decade inductive voltage divider (BIVD) in an automatic IVD bridge. New detection and injection circuitry was designed and used to evaluate the IVDs with either the input or output tied to ground potential. In the audio frequency range the DIVD and BIVD error patterns are characterized for both in-phase and quadrature components. Differences between results obtained using a new error decomposition scheme based on structural modeling, and measurements using conventional IVD standards are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Self-calibration of six-port reflectometers using active loads
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An automatic method for self-calibration of six-port reflectometers is reported in this paper. It is based on active load synthesis of well distributed standards over the Smith Chart. The advantages of this self-calibration method are: the setup is completely autonomous during the operation, measurement errors caused by the frequent connecting and disconnecting of calibration standards are avoided, the method is suitable for low and high frequencies, where sliding shorts are difficult to manufacture, as well as it simplifies operation of six-port reflectometers to non-specialized users.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A measuring system for in-situ calibration of high voltage transformers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A mobile calibration system for in-situ calibration of voltage transformers is analysed with respect to measuring uncertainty under field conditions. The total basic uncertainty is better than /spl plusmn/0.015% respectively /spl plusmn/0.3 mrad. The system has been used to calibrate 570 capacitor voltage transformers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Airborne radar in-flight antenna pattern testing
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper discusses the operation, the accuracy considerations, and the measurement process of an in-flight radar antenna pattern measurement. The in-flight tests performed for the Joint STARS multifunction airborne radar are summarized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Corrections to hyperfine splitting and Lamb shift induced by diagrams with second order radiative insertions in the electron line
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Contributions to HFS and to the Lamb shift intervals of order /spl alpha//sup 2/(Z/spl alpha/)/sup 5/ induced by a gauge invariant set of nineteen topologically different graphs with two radiative photons inserted in the electron line are considered. Corrections both to HFS and Lamb shift induced by nine diagrams are calculated in the Fried-Yennie gauge.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: European two-way satellite time transfer experiments using the Intelsat (VA-F13) satellite at 307/spl deg/E
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A Two Way Satellite Time and Frequency Transfer (TWSTFT) experiment performed between six European laboratories is reported. The characteristics of the time transfers undertaken between each pair of laboratory earth stations has been determined. Multiple time transfer and ranging experiments were performed to determine both systematic errors and delay instabilities in the TWSTFT system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new PTB reference RF-field sensor up to 1 GHz compared to metrological characteristics of commercial sensors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: From calibration data of commercial RF-field strength meters (radiation monitors) the state-of-the-art of measurement uncertainty due to anisotropy, non-linearity, range selection, and modulation response is compared to the prototype of a new PTB broadband RF-field sensor showing improved isotropy and frequency response.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The present watt balance: a measure of its resolution
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: It was possible to operate the watt balance in the normal mode, but with the magnetic field reduced by more than six orders of magnitude. This mode of operation allowed the investigation of possible sources of systematic errors not specifically connected with the magnetic field, but rather with the balance environment. This measurement revealed a general lack of environmental effects and indicated an upper limit of resolution less than thirty parts per billion for a potential watt evaluation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Large signal load-pull measurements using six-port reflectometers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes an active load-pull measurement system, using two six-port junctions for nonlinear characterization of power transistors. Load-pull measurements on a 600 /spl mu/m MESFET have been performed at 2 GHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spatial variations of field polarization and phase in microwave cavities: application to the cesium fountain cavity
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Wall losses in microwave cavities induce spatial phase variations in all held components. These variations depend on the component and can often be studied separately for each component by the use of suitable transmission line models. By a complete electromagnetic approach the phase relation between different components can be easily found, along with spatial variations, and it can be pointed out that in the presence of losses the vector field polarization is no longer linear, but becomes elliptic and point dependent. In this paper this new way of looking at the effects of wall losses in metal cavities is discussed, as it may become relevant in the context of the study of cavities for atomic frequency standards. In fact, circularly polarized fields can excite different atomic transitions than linearly polarized ones. Another detail which can be studied by electromagnetic calculations, as opposed to transmission line models, is the localized effect of the source on phase and polarization in the neighbourhood of the feed. Useful approaches to this more complex problem are outlined in this paper, and preliminary results are given for the case of a cylindrical TE/sub 011/ cavity, recommended for use in a cesium fountain frequency standard.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Detection optimization of disbond in layered composites with varying thicknesses using an open-ended rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The detection of air disbond in layered dielectric composite, which is an important practical issue in many industries, is studied both theoretically and experimentally. Sensitivity of disbond detection depends on certain parameters, like the frequency of operation, the distance between the sensor and the first dielectric layer, and the layered composite geometry (conductor backed or terminated by an infinite half-space of air). The impact of all these parameters is investigated theoretically and then verified experimentally.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Progress in absolute determination of /spl Phi//sub 0/ using superconducting magnetic levitation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Superconducting magnetic levitation system for the determination of magnetic flux quantum has been improved significantly in flux-up system using Josephson voltage. Studies are also in progress to improve mechanical measurement relevant to the floating body toward sub-ppm level uncertainty.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Trapping and laser cooling of Ca/sup +/ ions toward future optical frequency standards: observation of clock transitions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Experimental results of trapping and laser cooling of Ca/sup +/ ions for future optical frequency standards are reported. Ca/sup +/ ions were trapped and laser-cooled to below 1 K. To observe the electric-quadrupole-allowed transitions (clock transitions), the laser diode operated at low temperature was developed. With this laser, the clock transitions were observed using the shelved electron double resonance method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved optical frequency standards at 612 nm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Using FM spectroscopy as the detection method in an experiment of optical saturation absorption, a fractional stability (Allan variance) of 5/spl times/10/sup -14/ has been observed for an integration time of 10/sup 3/ s,and a reproducibility better than 1 part in 10/sup 11/ has been achieved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical double-resonance on single cold ions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Resonance on a weak signal line of a single cold ion appears at the maximum rate of intermittent quenching the fluorescence on a resonance line: The m=0/spl rarr/0 ground state hyperfine transition of a single /sup 171/Yb/sup +/ and the S/sub 1/2 /-D/sub 5/2/ quadrupole line of /sup 138/Ba/sup +/ may control a 12.6-GHz oscillator or 1.76-/spl mu/m laser, respectively, with less than 10/sup -16/ inaccuracy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Monitoring the 1 /spl Omega/ standard resistor by quantum Hall effect
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Resistance standards at ETL are maintained by quantum Hall effect. Resistance of the 1 /spl Omega/ resistor named 69J101 is monitored. The result is R69J101=1-(5.682/spl plusmn/0.018)/spl times/10/sup -6/+(0.110/spl plusmn/0.003)/spl times/10/sup -6/ t /spl Omega/ where t is time in years from Jan. 1, 1994. The difference of 1 /spl Omega/ standard between ETL and BIPM on 1990 international comparison is reduced from MINUS/0.128 ppm to -0.044 ppm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Density and polarisability of helium gas and the Boltzmann constant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Recent experimental and theoretical values of the refractive and dielectric properties of a macroscopic gas of helium and corresponding microscopic parameters such as the atomic (or molecular) polarisability lead to more accurate gas density determination as exemplified by an estimate of the Boltzmann constant.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SMILETRAP-a wide range high precision mass spectrometer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A Penning trap mass spectrometer designed for precision measurements of externally injected ions of almost any element and various charge states is described. Variability of the charge state allows high accuracy mass comparisons across the entire stable nuclear chart at the same or similar q/A ratio which is a measuring situation less influenced by systematical errors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the development of the rubidium frequency standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Factors defining the rubidium frequency standard stability are discussed. Using a cell with volume of 1 cubic cm, cell-filter with volume of 0.5 cubic cm and lamp with volume of 0.2 cubic cm, it is possible to realize high quality characteristics for a discriminator and the frequency standard as a whole.
