The volume of the rubidium-cell frequency standard can be reduced up to the value less than 200 cubic cm while maintaining reasonably high accuracy characteristics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stability transfer of stabilized Ar+ laser on optically pumped I/sub 2/ laser. Towards frequency standard around 1,3 /spl mu/m
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A Doppler-free stimulated-emission technique using an optically pumped I/sub 2/ laser with applications in spectroscopy and infrared frequency standards is reported. A single mode cw argon ion laser, locked on a hyperfine component of the 13P(43-0) /sup 127/I/sub 2/ line, is used as laser pump. Continuous wave oscillation is observed on transitions belonging to the B-X system into highly excited vibrational levels of the ground state. The long term stability of the argon laser (/spl Delta/v/v/spl ap/10/sup -13/ in 100 s) can be transferred on the iodine laser.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: International comparison of /sup 127/I/sub 2/-stabilized He-Ne lasers at /spl lambda/=633 nm using the third and/or the fifth harmonic locking technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An international comparison has been carried out of /sup 127/I/sub 2/-stabilized helium-neon lasers at /spl lambda/=633 nm from the CMI and the BIPM using the beat frequency technique. The lasers were stabilized by the third (THT) and/or the fifth (FHT), harmonic locking technique. Using the FHT, the frequency of lasers is shifted to higher frequencies. An iodine cell designated JM-03 was used to evaluate the frequency shifts produced by weaker components of the rotational-vibrational transition P(33) 6-3 in the mixed molecule /sup 127/I/sup 129/I. Laser comparison shows that the frequencies of components d, e, f, g of the R(127) 11-5 of the molecule /sup 127/I/sub 2/ are very strongly influenced by the weaker spectrum of components of the mixed molecule.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Very-high Q microwave resonances in trapped /sup 171/Yb/sup +/ ions: application as a microwave frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The 12.6 GHz microwave resonance in /sup 171/Yb/sup +/ ions confined in a linear Paul trap is interrogated using a cryogenic sapphire resonator-based microwave source. Line Q factors of up to 1.1/spl times/10/sup 13/ have been observed. We report on the performance of the ion trap-sapphire resonator system as a prototype 12.6 GHz frequency standard.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The new solar radio spectrograph at Hiraiso
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A wide band radio spectrograph (25-2500 MHz) for monitoring the Sun has been established at Hiraiso, Japan. A new data processing algorithm that removes interferences due to radio, television and other artificial signals from the raw spectrum data has significantly improved the signal to noise ratio of the spectrogram.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The accurate measurement of a micromechanical force using force-sensitive capacitances
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A sensor for the precise and accurate measurement of micro-mechanical forces is presented. The sensor is used to detect a tactile image and has capacitive force sensing elements which are detected by charge readout. The mechanical performance of the force sensor is evaluated and verified with experiments. The force-to-deflection and deflection measurements have been separated in order to result in a sensor structure in which the response is linear with force and little affected by fringe fields. The sensor is 0.25 mm/sup 2/ in size, it has a force range of 0.25 mN and a capacitance of 2 pF. The amplifier detects capacitance changes of 15 fF with a maximum non-linearity of 0.01% over the 1.25-2.5 pF range.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Set of high-quality corrugated resonators for measurements at millimeter-wave band
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A general-purpose set of six high-quality resonators for the band 32/spl divide/405 GHz has been designed. The resonators described are cylindrical cavities with corrugated side surfaces. The loaded Q-factor of (0.6/spl divide/1.0)/spl times/10/sup 5/ at SWR/spl les/2.0 has been achieved. The resonators can be used for measurements of signal fluctuations, constitutive parameters of substances, etc.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Determination of the Rydberg constant by direct frequency measurement
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have performed a pure frequency measurement of the 2S8S/D two photon transition in atomic hydrogen, without any interferometry. The hydrogen frequencies are compared with the difference of two optical standards, the methane stabilized He-Ne laser and the iodine stabilized He-Ne laser. In this way, an optical frequency of atomic hydrogen is directly linked for the first time to the cesium clock. We deduce a new value for the Rydberg constant with an uncertainty of 2.2 parts in 10/sup 11/. This value is currently the most precise available.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measuring the fine structure constant, /spl alpha/, using helium fine structure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The fine structure of the 2/sup 3/S-2/sup 3/P transition in helium has been precisely measured using laser excitation of an atomic beam. The results give /spl alpha//sup -1/=137.035853(3)(7)(99). The three values of standard deviation are from, respectively, the measured transition frequency, the frequency calibration, and helium theory (1978 value).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measuring amplifier noise on a noise source calibration radiometer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The complex noise parameters of amplifiers and other active devices are measured on radiometers designed to calibrate noise sources. A summary of the method is presented together with a set of results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 1.4-1.7 /spl mu/m, <2 ps white pulse generation for multiwavelength pulse source using supercontinuum in a single-mode optical fiber
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A white pulse laser source which outputs <2 ps pulses with peak powers >1.1 W over a spectral range from 1.4 to 1.7 /spl mu/m is presented. It is based on supercontinuum generation in a single-mode optical fiber pumped at the near-zero-dispersion wavelength by a subpicosecond pulse from an Er/sup 3+/-doped fiber ring laser.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: LPTF frequency synthesis chain: results and improvement for the near future
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have measured the frequency of the He-Ne/I/sub 2/ laser starting from the Cs referenced CO/sub 2//OsO/sub 4/ laboratory standard. As the laser diode stabilized on the two-photon transition in Rb seems to be a suitable reference for spectroscopic studies (H, He...) and a promising standard, we are modifying our chain in order to measure frequencies around 780 nm and specially the Rb one.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New results of absolute measurement of unperturbed frequency of F/sub 2//sup (2/) P(7)/spl nu//sub 3/-transition in methane with accuracy of 10/sup -13/
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The results of measurement of absolute shifts of recoil doublet components due to the influence of second-order Doppler effect, and mutual influence of their wings has been reported. Measurements were carried out using the unique laser spectrometer on the wavelength of 3.39 /spl mu/m with resolution of 10/sup -13/, and the optical clock. New results of absolute frequency measurements of 7-6 F/sub 2//sup (2)/ P(7)/spl nu//sub 3/-transition of methane with accuracy of 10/sup -13/ are presented. Possibility of increasing accuracy of these measurements to 10/sup -14/ been discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Accurate CO/sub 2/ laser frequencies and molecular constants of regular and new hot-band lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new, high-resolution, highly efficient, cw, CO/sub 2/ laser oscillating on more than 250 lines including over 40 lines in the new 9 /spl mu/m hot band has been built at NIST, Boulder. The frequencies of the 9 and 10 /spl mu/m hot band lines and high J (to J=66) regular band lines of /sup 12/C/sup 16/O/sub 2/, which now fill the gap between the 9 and 10 /spl mu/m regions, have been locked to saturated fluorescence signals in CO/sub 2/, and measured. New molecular constants and more accurate frequencies of the four common isotopes of CO/sub 2/ have been obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High stability current control in the 10 A range
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper reports the design and the evaluation of an high stability current source developed for energizing the C-field magnet of the high field cesium standard experiment, currently in progress at Politecnico di Torino. This source, devoted to C-field uniformity measurements, supplies about 1 kW dc power with a current stability of about 10/sup -7/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Bandwidth enhancement of single-shot data acquisition systems by deconvolution of system response
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Procedures have been developed (Feb.1994) for enhancing the effective bandwidth of single-shot measurement systems. One procedure characterizes the transfer function of the measurement system hardware, and the other is a software compensation technique to deconvolve this transfer function from the acquired data. The example shown employs a Tektronix SCD-5000 Transient Digitizer, with a -3 dB bandwidth improvement of 4.5 times, to over 15 GHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cross conductivity standard for nonferrous metals at NIM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A so called "cross conductivity standard" based on a new principle developed from Thompson-Lampard Theorem (1956) has been established at NIM by the end of 1992. The conductivity range of the standard is approximately from 3% IACS to 100% IACS and with an uncertainty about 0.07%. By using an AC measuring system and a new method, the unknowns can be calibrated with an uncertainty of (0.1% /spl sigma/x+0.12% IACS).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A calibration method of microwave noise sources with different types of connectors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A method to calibrate a microwave noise source with a connector different from that of the standards has been proposed. This method requires two adaptors for mating the connector of the unknown to those of the standards and a radiometer. The measurement principle and a measurement equation are expressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high-temperature superconductor cryogenic current comparator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: NIST is developing a cryogenic current comparator (CCC) to operate at 77 K, using high-temperature superconductor (HTS) ceramic shields and a HTS-based superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) detector. HTS shielding at low magnetic field levels is probably sufficient for high accuracy measurements. Unshielded sections of the ratio windings may produce a significant error.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new wattmeter for traceable power measurements at audio frequencies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the development of a wattmeter designed for traceable power measurements to 30 kHz and above. A description is given of a technique, which uses the three RMS values of voltage, current and sum of voltage and current to measure power. The resulting system is based around an analogue signal processor, which provides signal ranging and isolation. The design of the signal processor includes several unique aspects. Traceability is achieved by characterization of each stage of the system, this together with the overall measurement uncertainties, are reported. The results of comparisons with other standards are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frequency stabilization of a diode laser using the Zeeman shift of saturated absorption spectra of the /sup 87/Rb atom
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Saturated absorption spectra of the /sup 87/Rb atom under the magnetic field of several tens of gauss were observed with a diode laser oscillating at 780 nm, and Zeeman splittings of the 5/sup 2/P/sub 3/2/ excited state of the atom were numerically calculated to obtain the spectra theoretically. Both of the spectra agreed well, and a Zeeman-shifted absorption line was used for the frequency stabilization of the diode laser.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study of a 196.0 THz (1529 nm) frequency standard based on an optically pumped rubidium vapor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We study the performance-of 196.0 THz (1529 nm) DFB lasers frequency-locked to absorption lines of a rubidium vapor optically pumped at 384 THz (780 nm). We describe a simple theoretical model giving the absorption profile of such a vapor. The measured frequency stability of two DFB lasers frequency-locked to these lines reaches a level of 8/spl times/10/sup -10/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A redetermination of the Newtonian gravitational constant at the Los Alamos National Laboratory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A redetermination of the Newtonian gravitational constant is nearing completion at the Los Alamos National Laboratory. The method used will incorporate both the techniques of Eotvos (1986) and Cavendish (1798), albeit with additional innovations. The philosophy behind the design, the instrumentation and preliminary data will be discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high-accuracy harmonic analyzer prototype eased on FAFT
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: FFT is widely used for determining the spectra of band-limited and non-band-limited signals from their sampled data. However, FFT is subject to the sampling theorem and there is the possibility of some forms of aliasing error and leakage error as well. With a 12-bit A/D, a high-accuracy harmonic analyzer prototype based on fast anti-aliasing Fourier transform (FAFT) is developed. Unlike FFT-based harmonic analyzer, FAFT based analyzer does not need the anti-aliasing filter, and thus the transfer errors of anti-aliasing filter are avoided. Main error sources of the prototype are quantization noise, transfer distortion of S/H circuit as well as the effects of non-zero width sampling pulse including its jitter It is shown that dynamic sampling accuracy of the prototype is better than O. 1% over a dynamic range more than 20dB.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An automated high-frequency inductive voltage divider
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have developed an automated 16-bit binary divider for use over the frequency range 5 kHz to 300 kHz. The divider has errors of a few ppm at 100 kHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A review of realizations and comparisons of Josephson array voltage standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This presentation will review realizations of reference standards of voltage based on arrays of Josephson junctions and efforts to compare the standards of different laboratories.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Feasibility study on an indirect quantum standard of the ampere
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An indirect quantum standard of current, based on the simultaneous use of the Josephson and quantum Hall effects, may help to achieve interesting results in fundamental experiments involving the determination of the elementary electrical charge e and of the Josephson and von Klitzing constants. A feasibility study of such a measuring system is proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fast stabilization of a CO/sub 2/ laser for a frequency standard at 10 /spl mu/m
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A CO/sub 2/ laser has been frequency stabilized to an OsO/sub 4/ transition with a control bandwidth of 10 kHz. The obtained spectral purity of the laser is 100 Hz. The realization of very accurate frequency standards and experiments of high resolution spectroscopy in the 10 /spl mu/m region are made possible by this source.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The gravitational force at mass separation from 0.6 m to 2.1 m and the precise measurement of G
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We present the results of a gravitational experiment which is based on a microwave resonator. The gravitational force of a test mass acting on the resonator is measured as a function of distance. No deviation from Newton's law has been found and the gravitational constant G has been determined with a relative accuracy of 2.2/spl times/10/sup -4/ to be: G=(6.6724/spl plusmn/0.0015)/spl times/10/sup -11/ N m/sup 2/ kg/sup -2/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesis of the frequency of the Ca intercombination line (/spl lambda/=657,5 nm)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Recently CIPM has recommended the frequency of the Ca-intercombination line at /spl nu/=455986240.5 MHz, determined interferometrically, for the realization of the metre. Based on the existing frequency chain at PTB to the infrared, we report on the realization of phase-coherent frequency multiplication steps from a CO/sub 2/ laser, phase locked to the Cs clock, to the Ca stabilized dye laser.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: One-way time transfer using geostationary satellites: evolution of the experiment on the satellite TDF2
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper presents the results obtained on common-view time transfer measurements using the TV satellite TDF2 between four French laboratories. Different methods have been used to eliminate the influence of the satellite residual motion with a final precision that can reach 10 ns. The accuracy has been assessed using an orbit provided by the CNES, that also tested orbit restitution based on the time measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spectroscopy of the 1s-2s splitting in muonium
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A measurement of the 1S-2S energy splitting by Doppler-free two-photon spectroscopy yields a value of 2 455 529 002 (33)(46) MHz, which agrees with QED theory within two standard deviations. The mass of the positive muon is derived as 105.658 80 (29) (43) MeV/c/sup 2/ from the isotope shifts in this transition to hydrogen and deuterium.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calibration of rf field strength meters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A BCR intercomparison of field strength meters was performed during 1991-1993 over the frequency range 100 kHz to 1000 MHz and field strength range 1 V/m to 10 V/m. Using different calibration techniques. Four field sensors, electric as well as magnetic, have been used. If certain procedures are followed, a calibration uncertainty of less than 1 dB can be obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: GPS time precision enhancement between Telecommunication Laboratories, R.O.C. and Communication Research Laboratory, Japan
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We discuss how to reduce the GPS time transfer errors between the TL and CRL. A portable GPS receiver was used to measure the GPS instrumental time delay error of TL. The theory, the simulation results, and the experimental results of the GPS antenna position error correction were also discussed. Finally, we measured the ionosphere delay at the TL.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonadiabatic heating in electron turnstiles and pumps
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: It is shown that for electron turnstiles and pumps based primarily on the Coulomb blockade effect, heating and therefore a loss of precision can arise at low temperatures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Uncertainty evaluation of the PTB primary clocks CS3 and CS4
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: At the PTB two primary cesium atomic clocks with a vertical atomic beam were constructed and put into operation during the last years. The contributions to the total uncertainty traditionally considered as being of relevance were determined. The observation of the clock data however, has revealed changes in the mean frequency slightly larger than the combined uncertainty of the clocks. This dilemma makes refined studies inevitable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power and energy meters and their calibration
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper has two sections. In the first section, a description of many details, and of many small but important items, introduced in the electronic circuitry of power and energy meters, is given. Also, the explanation is presented of how the reduction is achieved to voltage and current. The second sections deals with power and energy calibrators and with very accurate instruments built for national and other high precision measurement laboratories. The first section deals primarily with the analog electronic circuitry and the description of the systematic and other error origins. The second section describes the implementation of the digital circuitry and digital computation in the calibration of high precision instruments. As everyone is aware, the calibrators are instruments in which the control problems are essential. In this paper, the author explains his recent views regarding the feedback, error feedforward and error feedback methods, and compares the analog and digital approaches in the realization of these control strategies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A false balance avoidance transductor for measuring large DC currents
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An improved feedback-controlled transductor capable of automatically returning to its normal balance state about the real origin when getting stuck in the false balance state is presented. It can be applied to the case where a large difference exists between the measurand and the compensation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multi-variance analysis: last improvements and practical utilization
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The multi-variance analysis yields a better sensitivity for the measurement of the frequency noise altering the oscillators as well as an estimation of the measurement uncertainties. This method has been improved in order to measure simultaneously drift and noise coefficients and non-equally spaced timing sequences. We defined a new standard of time stability measurement which is used for classical clocks as well as millisecond pulsars.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of techniques for bonding wires to quantized Hall resistors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Three different techniques for mounting quantized Hall resistors with AuGe/Ni alloyed contacts were evaluated. The best quality and most robust samples were made by evaporating bonding pads that overlapped the alloyed contacts and the substrate, so that bonds could be made over the substrate rather than over the heterostructure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Intelsat two-way time transfer experiments between Japan, Korea and Taiwan
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the first two-way time transfer experiments using Intelsat Ku-band-satellites in eastern Asia performed by Communications Research Laboratory (CRL: Japan), Korea Research Institute of Standard and Science (KRISS: Korea) and Telecommunication Laboratory (TL: Taiwan) in 1992. The experiments are based on the recommendation of Conference Generale des Poids et Mesures (CGPM) in 1987. Also they are based on the international cooperation program between CRL and KRISS, and institute-level cooperation between CRL and TL. The experiments attained the short-term precision better than 1 ns, which is much better than conventional GPS time transfer. Long-term precision was not so good as short-term one. We discuss the reasons of the long-term instabilities. We can also established the procedures to use Intelsat satellites under the support of Intelsat Headquarters and each countries' common carrier agents.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Precise determination of the power transmission coefficient of low-loss passive linear two-ports by RF noise power and RF attenuation measurement techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper presents the results of precision measurements of the power transmission coefficient of low-loss passive linear two-ports. Two different measurement approaches were intercompared, using RF noise power and RF attenuation measuring techniques. The noise power approach is preferably applied for the detection of small changes in attenuation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interlocking Rogowski coils: a fool's transformer
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have constructed interlocking, air-core, toroidally-wound solenoids. In principle, there should be no coupling between these Rogowski coils (in the absence of return loop and capacitive effects). We have searched for a mutual inductance between two such interlocking coils and report preliminary results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parity-controlled charge modulation of the supercurrent in the single electron transistor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have measured the parity-controlled charge modulation of the supercurrent in a superconducting single electron transistor, at different magnetic field and temperatures. We observed the characteristic features of the poisoning of the supercurrent enhancement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Progress on the measurement of proton gyromagnetic ratio at KRISS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A measurement of the proton gyromagnetic ratio in water by low field method is in progress at KRISS and a brief presentation is given for the experimental apparatus and the related experiments.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calibration technique using new calculable standard for RF reflectometers fitted with GPC-7 connectors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper presents new developments made at NPL towards improving traceability for reflection coefficient at RF in 7 mm coaxial line. The developments involve the introduction of a new calculable standard which interfaces with a GPC-7 precision coaxial connector. Results are given illustrating the performance of the new capability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurements of high voltage impulses (400 kV): implementation of a calibration test procedure
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper deals with the implementation of a new chain of calibration for high voltage lightning impulses up to 400 kV. Firstly, the definition and the characterization of a reference measuring system were studied. Then, different methods and procedures have been developed. Finally, the implementation of a calibration test procedure is validated with a metrological point of view.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Laser cooling of a natural isotope-mixture of Yb/sup +/ stored in a RF trap
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We demonstrate laser cooling of a natural isotope-mixture of Yb/sup +/ stored in a RF trap. One of the three major even isotopes was directly laser cooled and other isotopes simultaneously trapped were sympathetically cooled.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effective efficiency measurement results conducted on a X-band thin film waveguide barretter mount developed at NPL, New Delhi
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Effective efficiency measurements have been conducted at 10.0 GHz using a single load microcalorimetric technique on a thin film primary standard waveguide barretter mount designed and fabricated at National Physical Laboratory, New Delhi. The same mount was taken to three National Laboratories, namely NIST, USA; KRISS, Republic of Korea; PTB, Germany for an international comparison of effective efficiency measurements. This paper briefly describes the techniques employed for the measurement of effective efficiency of bolometer mounts by these countries. The results of effective efficiency are reported and intercompared.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An automatic bridge for inductive voltage dividers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We describe an automatic, injection-type bridge for inductive voltage divider applications at low audio frequencies. We used it to self-calibrate programmable IVDs fabricated in house by an automated "boot-strap" procedure. It is the heart of our reference standard for ac voltage ratios as well as a calibration system for IVDs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Current developments in accurate AC-DC transfer measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Recent improvements in commercial AC instruments led to new activities in the field of basic standards for AC-DC transfer measurements. Current developments are discussed in this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Precision calculations of frequencies for Balmer's transitions in hydrogen and Rydberg constant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have calculated the Rydberg constant by frequency comparison of the transitions 2s-8s, 2s-8d in hydrogen with corresponding QED-calculations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of the device-width on the accuracy of quantization in the integer quantum Hall effect
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Using a cryogenic current comparator bridge (CCC), several Hall samples of different width were compared to check whether size effect may affect the accuracy of quantization in the integer quantum Hall effect (QHE). In the range from 1 mm down to 10 /spl mu/m we did not observe any width dependence of the Hall resistance. The difference between the quantized Hall resistances of the i=2 plateaus of the various samples was found to be smaller than the measurement uncertainty (typically at the ppb-level).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Does the gravitational "constant" vary as the square of the frequency of light used in its observation ?
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Schwarzschild's mass parameter (m) is related to the gravitational mass through the Newtonian potential. A frequency dependent metric yields a volumetric metric mass parameter which can be directly related through the density, but predicts that the gravitational constant (G) should be directly proportional to the observational light frequency squared. Experimental verification is suggested.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high quality 1-V Josephson series array developed at KRISS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: By combining the selective niobium anodization process (SNAP) and the image reversal technique (IRT) a new fabrication process of integrated Josephson series array has been developed at KRISS. The array containing 2520 Nb/Al/sub 2/O/sub 3//Nb tunnel junctions produced stable quantized voltage steps up to 2 V with stability times of more than 5-h.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Minimizing time dilation shift in Penning trap atomic clocks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The time dilation shift is expected to give the largest systematic uncertainty in an ion clock. We show that, in a Penning trap, it can be minimized if the ions are prepared in a special spheroid. The results apply directly for one ion species and approximately for sympathetically cooled systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Noise reduction in an optical interferometer for picometer measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An optical interferometer with the resolution of picometer level was developed. Several techniques are exploited to reduce the output fluctuation due to the thermal drift, and air movement. The short term noise performance was better than 3 pm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: FDTD analysis of open-ended dielectric sensors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The reflection coefficient of an open-ended coaxial line immersed in water and methanol is simulated using a modified FDTD code. Calculated values are compared with previously obtained moment method and experimental values. The effects of variations in the end of line geometry on the reflection coefficient are investigated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frequency comparison between Cs and Mg atomic standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report in this paper the frequency comparisons between UTC (IEN) and the Mg standard prototype performed during a period of 420 days. We shall also discuss the implications of our results on testing the time stability of an important product of fundamental constants (g/sub p/m/sub e//m/sub p/) as well as the local position invariance principle.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 1-V Josephson voltage standard at IEN
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In this paper we describe the measurement system for the 1-V Josephson voltage standard installed at IEN, which uses Josephson junction arrays, and the results that have been obtained in calibrating 1-V voltage sources so far.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A Josephson voltage standard in multichip technology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A Josephson voltage standard is described which exactly meets industrial needs and is cost minimized. A new frequency measurement strategy and a new layout of the Josephson tunnel junction monolithic are introduced. Commercial instrumentation is replaced by monolithic components. Semiconductor and superconductor monolithics are hybrid integrated in multichip technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of an AC/DC transfer system at the INTI
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the work done at the INTI in order to improve the AC/DC transfer system. Thermal voltage and current converters were constructed by means of serial and parallel arrangements of single junction thermal converters. The frequency response of both arrangements are presented as well as a description of the design of the high voltage resistors and shunts.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization of the layered dielectrics using an open-ended coaxial line sensor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper presents a non-destructive technique for characterizing the dielectric sheets. An open-ended coaxial line is used as an electromagnetic sensor for this purpose. The procedure is validated by experimental results at microwave frequencies for a couple of solid as well as liquid samples. Limitations of the technique are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Monitoring industrial voltage standards by transporting Zener references calibrated by ETL Josephson standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Industrial voltage standards were monitored for 2 years by transporting Zener references calibrated by ETL Josephson standard. Standards of two participants maintained by using Zener's 10-V output agreed with the ETL standard within 0.4 ppm. A standard of one participant maintained by using standard cells agreed within 1.2 ppm. Voltage transfer capability of Zener's 10-V output was 0.1 ppm, 1.018-V outputs was 0.4 ppm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Accuracy and calibration considerations for ground based sensing of water vapor in the stratosphere and mesosphere
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The water vapor monitoring system (WVMS) is a ground based broad band microwave (22.235 GHz) radiometer that analyzes emission spectra from the mesosphere to determine water vapor mixing ratios. This paper emphasizes the technical details of the instrument, experimental techniques, comparison of alternate techniques, and especially accuracy and calibration issues.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new optical wavelength ratio measurement apparatus: the fringe counting sigmameter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new compact and achromatic Michelson-type interferometer with a variable path difference is presented. This "fringe-counting sigmameter" allows one to measure optical wavelength ratios between two radiations emitted by stabilized lasers. Maintained in vacuum, this apparatus can determine wavelength/frequency laser radiation from 0.36 /spl mu/m to 1.5 /spl mu/m with a relative accuracy of 5.10/sup -9/, with the use of a reference stabilized He-Ne laser.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High sensitivity fiber-optic magnetic field sensors based on iron garnets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Ferrimagnetic iron garnet crystals form the basis of magneto-optic magnetic field sensors which offer high sensitivity, broadband frequency response, and fiber-optic compatability. Recent developments at NIST promise still greater performance for these sensors based on the magneto-optic Faraday effect. Specifically, new sensor head designs incorporating flux concentration devices and novel experimental iron garnet compositions demonstrate the potential for enhancing the sensitivity of iron garnet sensors by two to three orders of magnitude.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Portable He-Ne/CH/sub 4/ frequency standard on cold particles
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The data on investigation of metrological characteristics of transportable He-Ne/CH/sub 4/ frequency standard (/spl lambda/=3.39 /spl mu/m) with the long-term stability of 5/spl middot/10/sup -15/ are presented. As the frequency reference we used the second-order Doppler-free resonance of cold CH/sub 4/-molecules with the halfwidth of 5 kHz on the 7-6 transition of magnetic hyperfine structure of methane. The results of comparison of the laser frequency standard with the frequency of unperturbed 7-6 transition and cesium beam are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: BCR intercomparison of ac-dc current transfer standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The established ac-dc current transfer standards and measurement set-ups of EC, IEN, LCIE, PTB, SP and VSL were intercompared in the current range from 10 mA to 20 A and in the frequency range from 10 Hz to 100 kHz. An agreement within 10 ppm to 30 ppm was obtained up to 100 mA, degrading to 100 ppm at 1 A (100 kHz) and 70 ppm at 10 A (20 kHz) and 20 A (5 kHz).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigation of dc precise voltage sources for use as Zener transport standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: 20 precise compact voltage sources based on Zener diodes were manufactured. These sources were under investigation at measuring system in NPO VNIIFTRI during the year. A few sources with voltage drift less than 5 ppm per year and noise level lower than 100 nV in the frequency band of 0.01-10 Hz were selected for manufacturing of 4-channels dc voltage transportable reference standard. This reference standard was investigated by Russian I-V Josephson systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization of the InGaAs detector to be used as a radiometric transfer etalon
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Large area InGaAs detectors are characterized by spectral sensitivity, spatial uniformity and shunt resistance, in order to determine their abilities to be used as transfer etalons in place of germanium detectors for power measurements in fiber optics field. The paper shows the initial measurements on a 5 mm-diameter InGaAs detector prior to an ageing process which will be monitored with a six months measurement cycling period. The measurements show a kink in the spectral sensitivity curve at 1650 nm, far away from the 1550 nm region, a good spatial uniformity at 850 nm, 1300 nm and 1550 nm, and a shunt resistance of 35 k/spl Omega/ at room temperature.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High accuracy absolute laser powermeter calibrated over the whole range
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The main contribution to this laser powermeter is the capability of its detector to be electrically calibrated over the whole measuring range (0...100 W), with an accuracy better than 1%. This allows an improved accuracy in determining the second-order polynomial coefficients describing thermocouple electric response.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: International comparison of standard capacitors in Asia/Pacific metrology programme
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An international comparison of standard capacitors in the Asia/Pacific Metrology Programme (APMP) has been carried out. The standards laboratories of eleven countries have participated in the comparison. A new 10-pF capacitor was fabricated, and the commercial 100-pF and 1000-pF capacitors were modified for use as the travelling standards. This comparison started in July 1991, and is expected to be completed before April 1994.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Silicon lattice measurement with an X-ray/optical interferometer in a vacuum [Avogadro constant determination]
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new X-ray/optical interferometer (XROI) has been constructed at NRLM. One feature is reduction of errors in the displacement measurement. For this purpose, we made an optical interferometer for on-line measurement of guiding errors. We report the results of lattice spacing measurement in a vacuum with the upgraded instruments.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Update on crystal lattice measurements at NIST
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The NIST crystal lattice measurements include the lattice period measurement of a silicon sample using optical interferometry (XROI) and a lattice comparison facility using Laue diffraction (delta-d). Crystals validated by these measurements are used in angle measuring spectrometers to produce X-ray and gamma-ray standards. This summary describes progress and problems in both the XROI and delta-d measurements and presents lattice comparison results for seven samples destined for X-ray and gamma-ray diffraction measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Running and testing of Josephson voltage standard series arrays
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: It was found that the yield of the Josephson tunnel junction series arrays produced is limited by the test systems at present commonly in use to test and work them as voltage standards. We present a new voltage biasing system. It allows a junction-by-junction inspection of the array under test between zero and 10 volts with an excellent current resolution of 10/sup -7/ A and an excellent voltage resolution of 10/sup -6/ V.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Precise indirect measurements of quantized Hall resistance ratio R/sub H/(i=1)/R/sub H/(i=2) in GaAs-based sample
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Indirect measurements of the quantized Hall resistance /spl rho//sub xy/=R/sub H/(i) are carried out on the i=1 and i=2 plateaus for an AlGaAs/GaAs heterostructure cooled at 1.2 K under both directions of magnetic field. The mean value of the ratio R/sub H/(i=1)/R/sub H/(i=2) differs from the value 2 by +0.3 part in 10/sup 9/ with a combined relative uncertainty (1 /spl sigma/) lower than 3 parts in 10/sup 9/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A thermal watt-transfer standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper describes a transportable ac power and energy standard developed at VNIIM. Based on a thermal principle, the instrument performs ac-dc transfer and absolute power and energy measurements in the frequency range from 40 to 500 Hz. The ac-dc transfer accuracy is better than 10 ppm at unity power factor and better than 30 ppm at 0.5 power factor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automated quantum Hall resistance standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: For precision quantized Hall resistance measurements quantum Hall effect samples have to be checked according to the CCE-guidelines. To perform these checks an automated measuring system is described, which is able to examine and characterize various samples. With these measurements a calibration of a precision 10 k/spl Omega/ resistance standard is obtained with an uncertainty of better than 5/spl middot/10/sup -8/ (1 /spl sigma/) using a long-scale digital multimeter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Precision measurement of the hydrogen and deuterium 1S-2S transition with a phase locked laser frequency chain
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: To perform a fully phase coherent measurement of the hydrogen and deuterium 1S-2S frequency we have extended our laser frequency chain by four optical divider stages that are successively bisecting a remaining difference frequency of 1.1 THz down to 66.2 GHz for hydrogen (60.9 GHz for deuterium). The divided frequency can be counted directly by harmonic mixing on a Schottky-diode. As a result we expect an improved value for the Rydberg-constant and order of magnitude improvements in a measurement of the hydrogen-deuterium isotope-shift.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Realization and maintenance of the unit of capacitance with the PTB cross capacitor during the last ten years
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A precise realization of the unit of capacitance is important for both the determination of the Josephson and the von Klitzing constants. The main design criteria of the PTB's cross capacitor, the maintenance of the unit of capacitance over the last ten years and a special capacitance measuring bridge for tracing back the electrode capacitance in the volt experiment to Si units are described in this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A determination of the Avogadro constant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have determined the Avogadro constant N/sub A/ from measurements of the (220) lattice spacing, density, and molar mass of high-purity and near-perfect silicon single crystals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Precision interferometric frequency measurement of the 674 nm /sup 2/S/sub 1/2/-/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ transition in a single cold Sr/sup +/ ion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The narrow linewidth 674 nm /sup 2/S/sub 1/2/-/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ transition in a cold Sr/sup +/ ion confined within an rf Paul trap has been probed using an optically-narrowed 674 nm diode laser, offset-locked to a second diode laser stabilised to a high finesse low-expansion reference cavity. A preliminary interferometric frequency measurement of the /sup 2/S/sub 1/2/-/sup 2/D/sub 5/2/ transition will be presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved resistance comparison system at Gakushuin University and a new determination of the quantized Hall resistance in terms of the NML OHM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Improvements to the cryogenic current comparator and other aspects of the resistance measurement system at Gakushuin University have led to a new determination of the quantized Hall resistance in terms of /spl Omega//sub NML/ with reduced uncertainties. This determination leads to the result R/sub H/(GU 1992)=(1+0.008(33)/spl times/10/sup -6/)R/sub K/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: International comparison GT-RF 75-B3: reflection coefficient at 300, 600 and 1000 MHz in 75 ohm coaxial line
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This international comparison was organized at the 1975 meeting of the Groupe de Travail pour les Grandeurs aux Radiofrequences. Eight national standards laboratories agreed to participate in the comparison, representing Canada, Slovakia, Finland, France, Germany, Hungary, the Netherlands and the United Kingdom. The traveling standards circulated among the participants were three coaxial terminations fitted with GR900 75 ohm connectors having nominal reflection coefficient magnitudes of 0.00, 0.03 and 0.10.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The ITS-90 realisation. A survey

articleTitle: Developing an optical frequency standard at 532 nm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A frequency-doubled Nd:YAG laser is used to study the hyperfine structure of several rovibrational transitions in molecular iodine via modulation transfer spectroscopy. Comparison of two independent lasers stabilized onto separate hyperfine components allows characterization of the stability, reproducibility and possible systematic shifts with pressure and power.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cryogenic current comparator for QHR determination at NML
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A cryogenic current comparator is being developed at NML to give high accuracy comparisons of room temperature resistors and quantized Hall resistances. The comparator incorporates novel developments in the method of calibrating auxiliary currents and in the method of construction of the superconducting shielding around the comparator windings.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 1-V and 10-V Josephson junction array voltage standard at NIM
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A group of standard cell can be calibrated simultaneously and safely by the JJAVS via a Hg-Zn cell based dc voltage reference in three minutes. The total uncertainty of 8/spl times/10/sup -9/ and 5/spl times/10/sup -9/ are achieved at 1.018 V and 10 V level for Zener reference.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Intercomparison of two iodine-stabilized He-Ne lasers at /spl lambda/=543 nm
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An intercomparison of two /sup 127/I/sub 2/ stabilized 543 nm He-Ne lasers, recommended as length standards, has been made between DFM and PTB, and is the first international comparison of this kind of lasers reported so far. articleTitle: Electrical to mechanical power equation by voltage systems: oscillatory solutions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Some principle voltage-operated structures with a contactless moving electrode are shown, together with relations useful for feasibility evaluation. Application to oscillating-mass systems based on electrical levitation is considered. They allow the force balance and the current generation to be performed simultaneously, yielding power equations independent of gravitational acceleration.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive current sources and feedback applied to the cryogenic current comparator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A novel current source for the cryogenic current comparator (CCC) is presented which is adaptable to many coil, resistance and filtering configurations. The effect of both current feedback from the SQUID and voltage feedback from the detector are examined and incorporated into the design. The advantages of the new system are examined in terms of flux tracking, leakage, self checking, accuracy and flexibility. The system has been used at NRC over the resistance range of 1 /spl Omega/ to 1 M /spl Omega/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Noise performance and chopper frequency in integrated micromachined chopper-detectors in silicon
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Recent advances in silicon micromachining technologies enable the fabrication of single-chip optical chopper-detector systems with integrated readout circuits in silicon. The micron-dimensions of the thin-film chopper would allow operation at much higher frequencies compared to conventional choppers. A typical integrated chopper is composed of an electrostatically-actuated comb drive, which displaces a reflecting film over the detector to give alternating transmission and blocking of impinging light onto the integrated photodiode.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

The results show an agreement of 5 parts in 10/sup 9/ with an uncertainty (1/spl sigma/) of 3 parts in 10/sup 9/, mainly due to instability of the Zener references. The instrument uses a modified digital phase-sensitive-detection technique with the phase locked to a fixed value and the modulation period tracking the measured lifetime. Typical resolution of the system is 0.05% for slow decay (>500 /spl mu/s) and 0.1% for fast decay.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: RF-trap apparatus for optical frequency standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A novel RF (Paul) ion trap apparatus, capable of providing extremely tight confinement is described. Strong localization of trapped ions reduces an important source of noise when using the ions as an optical frequency standard. Alternative cooling schemes, which provide stronger localization than conventional Doppler cooling are also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

In addition, the technique allows the phase changes through the attenuator to be measured accurately at the high attenuation levels.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Significant improvements in the method to determine the absolute molar mass of silicon have been achieved and are reported. They enable one to reduce the uncertainty contribution of the molar mass to the uncertainty of a previously published Avogadro constant N/sub A/. articleTitle: A high precision comparison of the quantized Hall resistance of MOSFET and GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure devices [measurement units application]
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report comprehensive high precision direct and indirect comparisons of MOSFET and GaAs heterostructure quantized Hall resistors, and of steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 for heterostructure devices. We find no difference between the MOSFET and the heterostructure Hall resistance at a level of better than 1 part in 10/sup 9/ (ppb).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest

articleTitle: Cryogenic hydrogen maser
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have begun to develop a prototype cold hydrogen maser (CHM). The main features of this CHM, which is designed to operate in the pulsed mode at 4.2 K, is the use of low loss alumina for the fabrication of the microwave cavity in order to reduce the overall size. A numerical simulation was performed to find the dimensions of the microwave cavity required for the TE/sub 011/ mode to be at 1.420 GHz, and the model has been confirmed experimentally. The CHM is intended to be used as a flywheel frequency standard at the NPL with medium-term stability of one part in 10/sup 16/ or better.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A cesium fountain frequency standard: preliminary results
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Laser cooling of atoms has opened up new possibilities in the field of atomic frequency standards. A cesium atomic fountain, first proposed by Zacharias in 1953, is now feasible: the atoms, first cooled by six laser beams, are launched upward using laser light, pass once through a microwave cavity, continue their ballistic flight and then fall through the same cavity. The long time between the two microwave interactions leads to a Ramsey resonance much narrower than in conventional Cs clocks using thermal atomic beams. The stability and accuracy of such a cesium fountain are very attractive. The use of diode lasers to cool, launch and detect cesium atoms in a low cesium pressure cell allows the construction of a simple and reliable atomic fountain frequency standard. A fountain frequency standard is now in operation at LPTF. A Ramsey resonance as narrow as 0.8 Hz has been obtained. A few days of continuous operation are routinely obtained. In closed loop operation the fountain frequency standard is continuously monitored against a H maser allowing an evaluation of the accuracy of the device. The short-term frequency stability is about 5.10/sup -13/ /spl tau//sup - 1/2 / limited only by the frequency noise of the microwave source. We intend to present a preliminary evaluation of this new standard with a discussion of the major systematic effects which determine the accuracy. The expected accuracy is expected to be at 10/sup -14/ level. In addition, a description of the whole design of the cesium fountain is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Linking an automatic noise power measuring system to primary noise standards facilities: comparison of noise power measurements between PTB (Germany) and CMS (Taiwan, R.O.C.) in the radio frequency range between 2.0 GHz and 18.0 GHz
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper presents the results of a comparison program between PTB and CMS which was started to estimate the performance of an automatic broadband noise power measuring system to be used for precise calibrations of noise sources. Two aspects are discussed, the influences of ambient temperature, and the effective system noise temperature.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of heretofor unsolved electromagnetic simulation problems in high performance multichip modules and printed circuit boards: simulation and measurement of power plane noise and internal inductance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: As digital system clock rates have increased and risetimes have decreased, simple RC load delay calculations have proved inadequate for prediction of signal propagation on circuit boards, MCMs, and even high performance integrated circuits. Issues such as characteristic impedance, proper termination, crosstalk, and dispersion dominate interconnect design, have to be dealt with. Electromagnetic (EM) modeling in high performance systems has become an integral part of the design process. Specialized EM modeling tools are required to address the problems of high clock rate digital system design. Development of these specialized EM simulation tools requires extensive analysis of algorithms and their numerical implementation, to ensure that the appropriate electromagnetic effects are modeled in an efficient manner. The algorithms, mathematics, and implementations of EM simulation programs must be verified through a process of design, assembly, and testing of specialized physical structures. Two new algorithms are described from derivation through measurement and verification: accurate analysis of resistance and inductance for MCM interconnect; and equivalent models of power and ground plant noise both of these new algorithms require measurement data to verify their accuracy. In the case of inductance modeling for MCM interconnect, it was possible to utilize existing transmission line test structures, but new test techniques were used to precisely measure impedance over a range of frequencies. In the case of the power and ground plane model, a unique test vehicle was designed specifically to verify both the circuit and wave models, using a variety of time and frequency domain measurement techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of defocus on near-field measurement of fiber mode field diameters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An instrument has been built that measures the mode field profile of optical waveguides by the near field method. It has been used to measure the effect of defocus on fiber mode field diameters. The results obtained from measurements on two different fibers at two wavelengths are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spectroscopy of /sup 127/I/sub 2/ hyperfine structure near 532 nm using frequency-doubled diode-laser-pumped Nd:YAG lasers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Frequency-doubled diode-laser-pumped Nd:YAG laser can constitute an interesting optical standard around 532 nm. More than ten of /sup 127/I/sub 2/ lines can be observed inside the laser spectral range. Two independent systems, stabilized on one /sup 127/I/sub 2/ hyperfine component, are used to check the frequency long term stability for metrological purpose.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Absolute frequency control of a 1560 nm (192 THz) semiconductor laser locked to a rubidium absorption line interrogated by a second harmonic generated signal
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We demonstrated second harmonic generation from a 1560 nm DFB laser using a KNbO/sub 3/ crystal. The 780 nm beam was used to interrogate a Rb line and lock the DFB laser frequency. articleTitle: International comparisons at low voltage (0.001 V) and high voltage (100 V) in coaxial line at 30 MHz
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: At a frequency of 30 MHz, (i) two micropotentiometers (0.001 V) have been intercompared between ASMW, OMH, NIM, NIST, NPL (India), PTB, TF and (ii), in a second exercise two thermal converters (100 V) between NIST, NPL (India) and PTB.
