articleTitle: Ultralow-frequency design of the Wien bridge oscillator using switched capacitors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A Wien bridge oscillator using switched capacitors (SC) and its automatic gain controller were tested. Over the frequency range from 10/sup 2/ Hz to 10 /spl mu/Hz, the oscillation was stable and the frequency was proportional to the clock frequency of SC. The distortion factor and the rise time were also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Standards to support lightwave communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Lightwaves have been at the heart of many developments in communications throughout history. Perhaps the earliest example of a long distance communication link was a chain of bonfires or beacons. Certainly by the beginning of the 18th century optical telegraph networks spanned many countries within Europe. However, the greatest explosion in lightwave communication technology has occurred in the last two decades, advanced by the successful development of fibre optic technology. Fibre optic systems now form the backbone of a worldwide communications network and the uses of fibres in local area networks is growing rapidly. Despite the massive advances in the use of fibre optics, the technology and its application to communications are far from mature. The optical fibre transmission windows at 1300 nm and 1500 nm each have bandwidths in excess of 10 THz - almost 1000 times greater than the radio frequency spectrum used for broadcasting and communications. This enormous bandwidth will allow carriers, each at a different frequency, to be used within the same fibre thereby increasing its transmission capacity. Frequency standards are currently being developed to support frequency and wavelength division multiplexing. The current status of standards for lightwave communications is reviewed, the current advances in the field are discussed and future requirements for standards are identified.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The 1993 atomic mass tables and beyond
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: With a Penning trap technique applied to even short lived (few s) radioactive nuclides, masses of many isotopes of half a dozen elements have been determined with a precision of about 10 keV or better, which is sufficient for nuclear physics purposes. With time of flight methods applied to undecelerated particles (in the region below mass number 80) from bombarded targets, but also with more classical methods, masses of many nuclides far from beta stability have been improved, or measured for the first time. It is expected that extension of these methods will lead to further extensions and improvements. Information is given on the way in which the mass values in the tables have been derived from many thousands of measurements of masses and of nuclear reaction and decay energies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Systematic errors of long thin coaxial cables for the connection of four-terminal-pair devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Four-terminal-pair devices which must be operated at liquid helium temperatures can only be connected to the measurement setup with relatively long thin cables. This unfortunately leads to a large increase of the errors introduced by these cables. Some considerations are presented which allow these errors to be reduced as is necessary for precision measurements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization of photoreceivers used in lightwave instrumentation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: "Photoreceiver" is a general term describing a photodiode and associated control and processing electronics, used for optical-to-electrical conversion. Photoreceivers take the form of power meters, optical spectrum analyzers, telecommunication receiving systems, and many other instruments. Numerous specialized tests exist for photoreceivers, but this paper discusses five fundamental tests with broad applicability. These tests are spectral responsivity, dynamic accuracy, packaging structure, frequency responsivity, and polarization sensitivity. Emphasis is on procedures likely to be used for fiberoptic telecommunication test instruments, using standards obtained from NIST.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of laser diode sources for small-size Ca optical frequency standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Wavelength (frequency) tuning, coverage, and linewidth reduction characteristics of a visible laser diode (LD) operating near 656 nm at room temperature were investigated by using optical feedback from Littrow-type grating (LG). Frequency tuning coefficients on the grating angle, LD temperature, and injection current were found to be 1 THz/degree, 32.39 GHz/K, and 6.15 GHz/mA, respectively, using a InGaAsP visible laser diode.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Accuracy of the computer controlled laser frequency standards based on resolved hyperfine structure of a methane line
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We present 2-years results of frequency comparisons of the transportable He-Ne laser standards at 3.99 /spl mu/m stabilized to components of magnetic hyperfine structure (MHFS) of F/sub 2//sup (2/)-line of methane, and stationary laser using resolved recoil doublet. Absolute frequency measurements of the transportable laser have been made and this value was transferred to the stationary one. On the basis of theoretical model of the line shape the frequency of unperturbed transition have been calculated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frequency measurement of pure rotational transitions of H/sub 2/O from 0.5 to 5 THz
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Frequencies of H/sub 2/O pure rotational transitions from 0.5 to 5 THz have been measured with an accuracy of one part in 10/sup 9/ using a tunable far-infrared spectrometer. Measured frequencies of more than a hundred spectral lines provide an excellent wavelength and frequency calibration standard for the far infrared.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new determination of the gravitational constant G
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The numerical value of the Newtonian gravitational constant has been determined using cylindrically shaped masses and a static torsion balance with electrostatic compensation of the gravitational induced forces. The experimental set-up is described and the results are announced. There is a surprising deviation from the CODATA value.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High-frequency calibration of inductive voltage dividers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have constructed a semi-automated system for calibrating inductive voltage dividers (IVDs) in the frequency range 5-300 kHz, with a target measurement uncertainty of 1 ppm at 300 kHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Proton/electron mass ratio and the electron's "atomic mass"
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Summary form only given. The heart of the Penning trap mass spectrometer (PTMS) is a well-machined, quadrupole trap with hyperbolic surfaces of revolution formed about a common axis of symmetry. Equally as important from the point of view of precision, a strong magnetic field, aligned along this trap axis, must be highly stable and uniform. For our present solenoid, the long term drift is /spl sim/0.1-0.3 ppb/h and short-term fluctuations are <1 ppb. We are now using a quite uniform magnetic field (with B/sub 2/<2 G/cm/sup 2/). Also, a significant improvement in the X-band microwave system (multiplied up to 160 GHz) now allows us to use the relativistic mass shift (equivalent to /spl sim/-10 G/cm/sup 2/) in order to observe the electron's cyclotron frequency with a precision of /spl plusmn/5 ppb per measurement and with systematics that are expected to be at least an order of magnitude less than that obtained in our previous work. The comparison ion in this case is a fully stripped carbon atom such that the electron's atomic mass can be directly determined upon correcting for lost electrons and their binding energies. At the present time, our typical single measurement precision for the C/sup 6+/ cyclotron frequency is about /spl plusmn/1 ppb which yields a relative precision on the order of 0.2 ppb after a 24-h data-period. Altogether, the typical measurement precision of the electron/carbon comparison now exceeds 1 ppb (using about 100 h of data). To obtain m/sub p//m/sub e/, a comparison is made with the proton's atomic mass which has an accepted value with an accuracy of 0.5 ppb. Thus, an improvement in this important fundamental constant is expected to be an order of magnitude, limited only by our estimate of residual systematics.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermal wattmeter with direct AC/DC power conversion
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A thermal wattmeter with direct AC power to DC voltage conversion is described. A three-terminal thermoconverter (TTTC) is used for AC/DC power substitution. The TTTC enables simultaneous application of mutually independent current and voltage into the same heater and this way to force phantom power dissipation in this heater. The dissipated AC power is substituted by DC power in a self-balancing thermal bridge circuit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An original passive device for on-wafer noise parameter measurement verification
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Using a thin film technology, we have designed and fabricated a new passive device for on-wafer noise parameter measurement verification. The main feature specifying this device is the same order of magnitude for input-output reflection coefficients and for noise parameters, as for low noise MESFET or HEMT transistors. This new device is ideal as a verification standard, and suited for on-wafer measurements due to its small size and wide operation bandwidth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Broadband frequency measurement in the near infrared using point contact Schottky diode
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Results obtained from high order harmonic mixing between infrared lasers and microwave radiation in point contact Schottky diodes are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A measurement of Newton's gravitational constant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have measured the Newtonian gravitational constant using a compensated torsion balance in which the gravitational torque is balanced by an electrostatic torque from an electrometer. The electrometer is calibrated by accelerating the whole apparatus. Our result and uncertainties are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Picosecond time domain measurements using GaAs FET sampler
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Sampling measurements in the low tens picosecond range are performed using a hybrid FET technology which incorporates the different functions i.e. sampler, sampling pulse generator, test step generator. The accuracy of measured waveforms is investigated using time domain simulations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A U.S. intercomparison of Josephson Array Voltage Standards
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Qualification of intrinsic standards is a problem for laboratory accreditation systems. Accredited laboratories must demonstrate that their intrinsic standards actually provide the accuracy claimed. Ten standards laboratories have participated in an intercomparison of their 10 Volt Josephson Array Standards. The intercomparison program is described and results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Two-way time transfer experiments via meteor burst communication
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Meteor burst communication equipment has been successfully utilized in Russia for two-way time comparisons between standards of several time-keeping services. For its operation, the equipment depends on carrier phase measurements at several frequencies. Time transfer with accuracy better than 1 ns for a distance up to 2000 km is possible via this self-contained and low-cost equipment. To test the equipment and to estimate the time transfer performance, a series of time transfer experiments has been made on several meteor links in 1991-1993.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transformer bridge for the high-accuracy comparisons of standard resistors at low frequencies
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A transformer bridge has been developed at IMM for comparing low-value standard resistors. It is possible to compare resistors ranging from 0.1 Ohm to 100 Ohm. The sensitivity of bridge at 1 Hz frequency is less than 0.001 ppm at room temperature.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The 1s Lamb shift of hydrogen-like very heavy ions measured at an electron cooler
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Spontaneous capture of free cooling electrons by bare high-Z ions leads to the emission of X-rays. The distinctive features of this new X-ray source for precision spectroscopy of high-Z few-electron systems are demonstrated. They enable a determination of the 1s Lamb shift of hydrogenlike very heavy ions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Antenna standards and laboratories in Europe
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The goal of this paper is to present an overview on antenna standards and laboratories within Europe. In this context, Europe will be limited geographically to the member nations of the European Union (EU), formerly the European Community, and the European Space Agency (ESA). In addition to these two instances, other parallel organizations in this field exist such as the Western European Laboratory Accreditation Cooperation (WELAC), the Western European Calibration Cooperation (WECC) which includes EUROMET, the European Collaboration for Measurement Standards and the European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI). And lastly, there are the national standards organizations and laboratories.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A portable and stable source of AC voltage, current and power
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper describes a portable and stable source of AC voltage, current and power. It was developed for use with the NRC Transfer Standard to provide on-site calibrations of the watt and voltampere standards maintained by the metering departments of Canadian electrical utilities in order to establish traceability to the national standard of the National Research Council of Canada (NRC). The stability of the source monitored over 100 seconds, a typical measurement cycle of the Transfer Standard, is better than /spl plusmn/10 ppm for the voltage and current outputs. The stability of its AC power output is better than /spl plusmn/20 ppm, at all power factor settings.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Accuracy evaluation of the LPTF optically pumped primary frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The optically pumped Cs beam frequency standard under development in our laboratory was first evaluated in 1993. The short term stability was /spl sigma//sub y/(/spl tau/) is 5.5/spl middot/10/sup -13//spl tau//sup - 1/2 /. The accuracy has been estimated to 1.1/spl middot/10/sup -13/, mainly limited by the distributed phase shift. After modification of the cavity, a new evaluation is in progress and is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Accurate far-infrared rotational frequencies of carbon monoxide in excited vibrational states
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Pure rotational transitions of carbon monoxide in the excited vibrational states /spl upsi/=1 and /spl upsi/=2 of the ground electronic state have been measured in the 0.3 to 4.0 THz spectral region. Accurate center frequencies of 50 transitions with J values up to J=33 as well as improved sets of rotational constants are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 25 kHz-500 kHz, 0.001 to 0.75 power factor, 10 MW wattmeter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A multi-range instrument is described that measures-usually within 0.1%-voltages (100 V to 20 kV), currents (1 A to 1000 A), and powers (P.F.'s from 0.001 to 0.75) from 25 kHz to 500 kHz. Several novel zero power factor calibration techniques are proposed. Theory is confirmed by experimental results. Traceability is established.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Active probes for on-wafer millimeter-wave network analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Emerging mm-wave and high-speed fiber-optic applications will demand signal and network instrumentation with bandwidths beyond 1O0 GHz. We have developed nonlinear transmission line (NLTL) pulse generators and NLTL-based sampling circuits with bandwidths exceeding 500 GHz. For on-wafer parameter and waveform measurements, we have constructed active probes incorporating an NLTL-based network analyser IC and rugged, low-loss quartz coplanar-waveguide probe tips. Measurements are made with a pulsed (NLTL) stimulus signal with frequency information obtained by Fourier transformation. On-wafer measurements have been demonstrated to 200 GHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Systematic errors in NIST-7
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We describe a continuing, in-depth evaluation of NIST's new optically pumped frequency standard, in which all known sources of systematic error are investigated; most by two or more independent techniques. Additionally, we have used both analog (fast sine-wave modulation) and digital (slow, square-wave modulation) servo systems during the evaluation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Time transfer in India using satellite-TV signals in a common view mode
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: For the use of satellite-TV signals in a common view mode a detailed analysis relates the prediction errors of satellite co-ordinates to time comparison accuracy. It promises an accuracy better than two microseconds over India with the available quality of satellite ephemerides. The development of an automatic recorder for this purpose improves the measurement capability and its applicability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization of radiometer using 8-term linear model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A novel 8-term linear model for precision characterization of total power radiometer and for error corrected noise temperature measurements is presented. This model describes dependance of the effective noise temperature of noise source measured upon input mismatch, gain and the four noise parameters of the radiometer. Its validity has been verified experimentally.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurements on indoor reception of broadcast signals at 800 MHz
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes measurements on indoor reception of broadcast signals. The fading characteristics in the spatial and frequency domain are studied. Furthermore, an evaluation of the building attenuation loss is given. Theoretical explanations of the observed phenomena are also provided.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Operation method of three-gate single electron pump
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The polygon of equilibrium energy planes of a three-gate single electron pump in 3D gate voltage space is presented. Considering the trajectory in the 3D gate voltage space of the pump, stable operations are possible by applying sinusoidal gate voltages.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Achieving high precision in NMR flux density and /spl gamma/'/sub p/ measurements-accounting for the asymmetric line
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Flux density measurements via nuclear magnetic resonance differ from the average flux density because spatial variations of the flux density cause line-shape asymmetries which shift the measured frequency by a measurement dependent amount. A method has been devised for correcting for this effect and tested against theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automated calibration methods for a high-voltage Park divider
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We describe two new methods of calibrating a 100-kV Park divider, fitted with N/10 taps. They prescribed a series of automated measurements using (i) a digital conductance comparator, and (ii) a set of full-bridge circuits configurable entirely from the divider sections. Self-heating effects were studied systematically under PC control. Preliminary measurements determined the 1/10 ratio to /spl plusmn/25 ppm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sympathetic cooling of trapped ions with resonant laser radiation [frequency standard application]
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We propose a novel model to describe dynamic properties of ions that are cooled by collisions with other laser-cooled ions in a quadrupole rf trap. The limit temperature of the sympathetic cooling is estimated as functions of the trap and laser parameters, and the mass of the ions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Initial evaluation of the "bottoms up" time recovery technique
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes a new time transfer methodology and evaluates the performance of a number of globally distributed timing systems that utilize the technique. Active steering of high performance atomic clocks based on one-way GPS broadcasts is implemented automatically at remote sites. Data flows "up" to a central node where a series of processing and analysis steps provide after-the-fact calibration data. Using this technique, the widely separated sites can be inter-calibrated and their individual UTC time recovery performance can be monitored, managed and maintained. Relative synchronization between sites is as low as 2.5 ns over a 4000 mile baseline, and UTC(USNO) time recovery system wide is below 10 ns.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A contribution in replacing the kilogram by means of the voltage balance ETF
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper gives a short description of the basic principle of work of the EFT voltage balances, as well as the measurement procedures enabling the absolute determination of the volt. Recapitulation of the previous achieved measurement results and the estimation of expected uncertainties for the further experiments using the so-called charge-method, is also given. New measurement series have successfully started at the end of 1993.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measuring the gravitational acceleration by superconducting magnetic levitation system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Summary form only given. A method for the measurement of the acceleration of gravity, which is based on the fact that for fixed vertical position, the frequency of small mechanical oscillations of a superconducting levitated body placed in the nonuniform magnetic field of a coil energized by a direct current is independent of the levitated mass, is proposed. Peculiarities and errors of the method are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New RF and microwave metrology at PTB
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: During recent years, the demands for calibrations of RF power, attenuation, voltage and reflection coefficient standards have increased considerably, mainly by industrial calibration laboratories of the DKD (Deutscher Kalibrierdienst). Some new developments to cover these requirements are presented in this paper.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Corrections of order /spl alpha//sup 2/(Z/spl alpha/)/sup 5/ to the Lamb shift in hydrogen
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Contributions to the Lamb shift of order /spl alpha//sup 2/(Z/spl alpha/)/sup 5/ induced by all diagrams with closed electron loops are obtained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: DC and AC quantum Hall measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The quantum Hall effect (QHE) is now widely used by national laboratories to establish a reference standard of DC resistance featuring low uncertainty with respect to the ohm and very high reproducibility. For high quality QHE samples, the reproducibility of the quantized Hall resistance (QHR), measured at DC or at very low frequencies (of order 1 Hz), is of order 1 part in 10/sup 9/. Accurate resistance-ratio measurement techniques have been developed to calibrate conventional resistance standards (in particular 1 /spl Omega/, 100 /spl Omega/ and 10 k/spl Omega/ standards) in terms of the QHR, with uncertainties not higher than a few parts in 10/sup 9/. The following techniques are reviewed: DC cryogenic current comparators bridges, low frequency AC cryogenic current comparator bridges and low frequency AC bridges using high permeability magnetic cores and operating at room temperature. Sources of uncertainties and limitations in the resolution of the measurements are discussed. The technique of connecting QHE samples in series or in parallel using multiple links is discussed. Another possible metrological application of QHRs would be to use them, at frequencies of order 1 kHz, as references of AC resistance for the calibration of capacitance standards, the link between the resistance and the capacitance being made using a quadrature bridge. The techniques used for these investigations are discussed, in particular the use of coaxial AC bridges for measurements of QHRs considered as four terminal-pair impedances and for the evaluation of the residual longitudinal resistivity of the samples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesis of cyclically symmetric five-ports
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A class of matched, symmetric five-ports have been synthesized by solving the circular cylindrical wave equation. Among the solutions are chosen those for which the match condition is fulfilled over the broadest bandwidth. Bandwidths up to +/-20% have been found.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurements and analysis of the frequency stability of GPS Navstar clocks
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Analysis of the frequency stability of Global Positioning System (GPS) on-orbit Navstar clocks is performed by the Naval Research Laboratory (NRL). Clock offsets for each Navstar clock are derived from smoothed pseudorange measurements collected as the Navstar space vehicle passes over the tracking station. The clock offsets are further smoothed and estimated at the time of closest approach (TCA) of the space vehicle over the tracking station. Analysis of more than 50 Navstar clocks by NRL shows that the majority of these clocks provide performance that exceeds the GPS frequency stability specification. This precision measurement technique is capable of determining one-day frequency stabilities of the Navstar GPS clocks to an accuracy of better than 1/spl times/10/sup -13/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A microwave technique for measuring three-phase saturations in cylindrical cores
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A microwave instrument for measuring oil, air and water three-phase saturations in cores was proposed in this paper. According to the principle of microwave transmission, a special-designed microwave transducer was used. The instrument is made of X-band waveguide components and devices. The measurement errors of the instrument are less than /spl plusmn/0.03.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distribution of dielectric relaxation times and the moment problem
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A procedure for deconvolving time-dependent distribution functions from permittivity data is developed. The problem is reduced to solving an associated moment problem using a maximum-entropy procedure. The method is applied to synthetic permittivity modeling both for in-band and out-of-band regions. The numerical results indicate that the technique has potential for deconvolving the distribution function from the permittivity data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The extended-least-squares treatment of correlated data
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A generalization of the extended-least-squares algorithms for the case of correlated discrepant data is given. The expressions of the linear, unbiased, minimum-variance estimators (LUMVE) derived before are reformulated. A posteriori estimates of the variance taking into account the inconsistency of all of the experimental data have the same form as for the case of non-correlated data. These estimates extend the previous improvement on the "traditional" Birge-ratio procedures to the case of correlated input data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 10 V calibration system using 1 V Josephson array at KRISS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A 10 V calibration system at KRISS is described which allows the measurement of 10 V electronic voltage standards using 1 V Josephson array with the help of an automated 10:1 resistive voltage divider system. The overall uncertainty of a measurement (1/spl sigma/) at 10 V is less than 0.1 ppm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A broad-band time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A time domain spectroscopy is applied to an efficient and broad band measurement of electrical properties of biological substances. Observed reflected waves by a time domain reflectometer from beef meat were analyzed by a time domain analysis covering from dc to 10 GHz. A computational technique has been developed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The coplanar waveguide (CPW) technique for wideband dielectric measurement: a new concept
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A novel concept stemming from the coplanar waveguide (CPW) technique is proposed for wideband dielectric measurement in the frequency range up to millimeter-waves. The new approach uses surface fields of the coupled CPW slots which interact dynamically with lossless or highly lossy material under test. In this work, some preliminary theoretical and experimental results indicate a promising wideband sensibility for different material samples, thereby giving rise to a new possibility in dielectric measurement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high precision dc voltage measurement system in JJAVS
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Some methods are taken in the high precision dc voltage measurement system of JJAVS, including the low thermal emf scanner, especially designed cable, the Hg-Zn cell based voltage reference, the executed program as well as a suitable calibration procedure. Results show that uncertainty of dc voltage measurement system is 5 nV.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Using the modified measuring setup at the PTB
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: In the past several improvements in the experimental setup for the determination of /spl gamma//sup 1//sub p/ have been realized in order to reduce the measuring uncertainty. The various improvements are reviewed and the latest result obtained with the new setup are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 30 MHz-1000 MHz half-wave dipole antenna calibration system in anechoic chamber
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The half-wave length resonant dipole antennas calibration system for 30 MHz to 1000 MHz using comparing method with standard antennas in an anechoic chamber has been developed with error less than /spl plusmn/2.5%. The errors in the system are considered and evaluated experimentally.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a clamp-on magneto-optical current transducer for power systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new type of Faraday effect based magneto-optical current transducer (MOCT) has been developed. This paper presents the theoretical background, engineering design, and rest results of this MOCT. The sensor uses a clamp-on design and avoids the need to break the current carrying circuit in order to have the conductor enclosed by the optical path. The MOCT has two output stages; 1 KA, and 20 KA, so that it can provide current signals for both power system metering and relaying devices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prototype of a large ring laser for geoscientific applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Optical ring cavities to measure rotation in geoscientific applications require quality factors 10/sup 10/<Q<10/sup 14/, and perimeters of over 1 m. The prototype that has been transferred into a cave has 3.5 m perimeter and Q>10/sup 10/. The line center due to the Sagnac effect of the Earth rotation (about 70 Hz) has at present an error of about 5 /spl mu/Hz, i.e. a relative precision of 1.0/spl times/10/sup -20/ is achieved, using the 633 nm HeNe laser line.<<ETX>>

articleTitle: Construction of CCC resistance ratio bridge
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper introduces the cryogenic current comparator (CCC) resistance ratio bridge being built at DFM, which is designed to relate the value of quantized Hall resistance R/sub H/(i) to room temperature resistance standards. The CCC is an overlapping tube type with copper wire. A double constant current source is used to supply for the CCC resistance ratio bridge.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The performance and reliability of NIST 10-V Josephson arrays
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper reviews eight years of fabrication of 10-V Josephson array chips at NIST and the performance and reliability of these chips at 22 different standards laboratories. Failure mechanisms and statistical data on failure rates are presented for devices made with both Nb/Nb/sub 2/O/sub 5//Pb and Nb/Al/sub 2/O/sub 3//Nb junctions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high-speed TVC system for full-range AC traceability
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A difficult and important region in the AC traceability chain lies in the higher voltage ranges from 30 volts to 1000 volts at frequencies between 100 kHz and 1 MHz. This paper describes recent developments to improve the accuracy/speed performance of AC voltage buildup over these ranges.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An ac/dc active attenuator for comparison of TVC with different input voltages
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper describes a system for generating two voltages in a well-established ratio to be used for direct comparison of thermal voltage converters having different nominal voltages.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transportable dc voltage standard based on commercially available Zener diodes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A high-quality transportable dc voltage standard has been composed using glass packaged Zener diodes which are placed on the market. The stability is shown to be better than 2 ppm/year at the levels of both 10 V and 1.018 V.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ZnSe magneto optic sensor for measurements of 50 Hz to 100 Hz magnetic fields
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A bulk ZnSe magneto optic sensor, designed for 50 Hz to 100 Hz field frequencies. With a 633 nm HeNe source, is described. Practical results obtained from the sensor are compared with a simulation model. Data pertinent to the design of ZnSe sensors fur various applications as well as suggestions for the improvement of sensitivity are also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calcium optical frequency standard
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We report on high-resolution spectroscopy with dye and diode lasers and with three different samples of Ca atoms, in an effusive beam, in a laser cooled beam, and in a magneto-optical trap. The results should allow to improve the Ca, optical frequency standard, recommended by the CIPM, with a relative uncertainty below 10/sup -14/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Photonic electrode-less passive electric field sensor
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A novel Mach-Zehnder interferometric wideband electric field sensing device utilizing the electro-optic effect is reported. Reverse poling of one arm of the interferometer allows for a response to common-mode electric fields. Because the lithium niobate sensor uses no metallic electrodes, there is only minimal disturbance to the field being measured.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent developments in RF and microwave dielectric measurements at the UK National Physical Laboratory
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Microwave dielectric measurements commenced at NPL in the late 1960s. Instruments developed under that programme-TE/sub 01/-mode cavities and open resonators-remain in use today because they provide the most sensitive means of measuring very low dielectric losses in the frequency range 10-144 GHz. More recently, in the mid-1980s, a programme of very high loss materials measurements commenced which was originally concerned with biomedical applications but which has been extended to the characterization of foodstuffs, various polar dielectric liquids and radio absorbing material (RAM). A major concern in all of this work has been the requirement to ensure that measurements are demonstrably traceable to national standards: usually impedance, attenuation or dimensional standards are the most relevant. Another important aspect of the work is the estimation and reduction of measurement uncertainties. In pursuit of these aims the laboratory has always sought to take part in measurement intercomparisons both at local and international levels. NPL is the pilot laboratory for a BIPM intercomparison of complex permittivities of polar reference liquids. A third aspect of the work is to extend existing techniques to enable them to perform measurements upon new types of sample or to cover different ranges of complex permittivity. This can be a very cost-effective way of expending measurement capability since it usually does not involve gross expenditure on new instrumentation. These aspects of the work are illustrated in this review by reference to three recent dielectrics projects undertaken at NPL.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and performance evaluation of the NIST digital impedance bridge
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An impedance bridge that compares two-terminal standard inductors to characterized resistors is described. A dual-channel digitally synthesized source and sampling digital multimeter are used to generate and measure relevant bridge signals. A linear interpolation algorithm is used to autocalibrate the bridge to a 1 nF air-dielectric capacitor. An intercomparison of the new bridge with existing measurement standards in the low audio frequency range for inductors 1 mH to 10 H is reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study of cryogenic current comparators with different SQUIDs
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: This paper describes the recent study of improvements of resistance bridges based on cryogenic current comparators at BNM/LCIE. Two new cryogenic current comparators were built with different commercial SQUIDs (RF, UHF and DC). Their current sensitivities and sources of noise are investigated. In addition, a direct comparison technique is developed to check large ratios of windings with a measurement uncertainty better than one part in 10/sup 9/(1/spl sigma/).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of the breakdown of the IQHE in wide GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The breakdown of the integral quantum Hall effect (IQHE) at high current is studied in wide high quality GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructures on the i=2 and i=4 Hall plateaux. Pronounced steps in the longitudinal resistance are observed with rich time structures, which are analyzed with different techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development and investigation of Nb-Al-oxide-Nb Josephson junction arrays [voltage standard application]
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: An array of 3072 Josephson junctions Nb-AlO/sub x/-Nb is developed at IEM "KVARZ". Some preliminary results of an investigation of I-V curves under microwave irradiation in the 70 GHz frequency band are given. Zero current quantized voltage steps are displayed up to 450 mV with an amplitude >100 /spl mu/A. An improvement of the fabrication process, which is in progress, will enable to increase quantized voltage steps region up to 1 V.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Tunable phase-locked diode lasers for precision spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We have developed an electronic circuit for phase-locking extended-cavity diode lasers to a stable reference laser. The basic phase-lock operates with input frequencies between 5 MHz and 1.5 GHz and allows synthesizer tuning of the difference frequency between the lasers. An external mixing stage can be used for an arbitrary frequency offset.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On a draft of a superconducting magnetic levitation system intended to monitor stability of the unit of mass
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Designing an electromechanical system of superconducting levitation as a combination of flat elements is suggested. A single element comprises a planar rectangular coil produced in photolithography technique and a plane located near and parallel with the coil. It can be used both as a lift couple and in a magnetic bearing. Characteristics of the element in both applications have been calculated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Absolute measurements of the densities of silicon crystals in vacuum for a determination of the Avogadro constant
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: Absolute measurements of the densities of 1-kg single-crystal silicon spheres have been performed for a determination of the Avogadro constant. A scanning type optical interferometer was used to measure the diameters of the spheres in vacuum, and the volumes were obtained by fitting the diameters to a series of spherical harmonics. Thickness of oxide layers on the surfaces of the spheres has been determined by using an ellipsometer to evaluate the effect on the density. Total uncertainties of the densities are estimated to be 0.1 ppm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The silicon (220) lattice spacing: analysis of a new measurement
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: A new experiment has been run for the past year at the IMGC to measure the (220) lattice spacing in silicon by X-ray/optical/interferometry. The data so far collected show that the experiment is capable of 5/spl times/10/sup -9/ resolution. A new determination of silicon d/sub 220/ is reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frequency dependence of some 100 /spl Omega/ resistors measured with a CCC-based AC resistance bridge
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The paper describes frequency dependence of some 100 /spl Omega/ standard resistors in the frequency range from 0.1 Hz to 1 Hz. The measurements are carried out with an automated ac bridge based on the cryogenic current comparator (CCC) and a dc SQUID null detector. A GaAs quantum-Hall resistance cooled down to 1.4 K-1.8 K was used as a reference. The plateau i=2 was obtained at 7.5 T. Some resistors such as a N.B.S. type 100 /spl Omega/ (L&N) reveal a strong frequency dependence below 1 Hz while the frequency dependence of the Wilkins type 100 /spl Omega/ (Tinsley) is barely visible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Josephson noise thermometry with HTS devices
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: We propose that devices based on HTS Josephson junctions may have a useful role in allowing one of the novel applications of LTS SQUIDs, as primary thermometry standards for the millikelvin range, to extend their range to above 10 K.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The 2/sup nd/ APMP resistance intercomparison
publicationTitle: Proceedings of Conference on Precision Electromagnetic Measurements Digest
abstract: The results of a recent resistance intercomparison carried out as part of the Asia Pacific Metrology Programme (APMP) will be given. Three 1 /spl Omega/ and one 10 k/spl Omega/ standards were used. Eight national standards laboratories participated, including some laboratories with quantum Hall resistance standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
